Apply scams or bait-and-switch outcomes to approximately 5–10% of generated listings, varying the chance by reputation, verification, broker quality, urgency, and risk. Do not make most jobs fake. Players may inspect, refuse, negotiate, investigate, choose surveillance, capture, extraction, exorcism, rescue, nonlethal alternatives, report the client, betray the broker, or change sides. Preserve player agency and fair warnings while allowing dangerous jobs to carry serious legal, faction, civilian, reputation, supernatural, and retaliation consequences.

call-for-help-combat-option.name: Call for Help Combat Option
call-for-help-combat-option.text: During a difficult combat encounter, offer Call for Help when the player has a plausible way to communicate or signal for assistance. Resolve it by selecting one random existing NPC from the current world roster who can reasonably respond based on location, distance, communication, faction access, relationship, availability, current injuries, active quests, legal status, and immediate danger. Do not invent a new helper when an existing NPC is selected. The response may be a temporary party join, rescue intervention, evacuation support, healing, shielding, restraint, investigation, or another relevant contribution; do not assume every responder is a combat specialist. The selected NPC arrives after a believable delay when circumstances permit and leaves after the encounter unless the player and NPC explicitly establish a longer arrangement. Call for Help is a safety valve, not a guaranteed win: it may fail in sealed areas, communication dead zones, surprise attacks, inaccessible locations, or when no existing NPC can reasonably respond. It should normally be available once per continuous encounter, and using it may create consequences such as a favor owed, delayed arrival, missed obligations, exposure of the player's location, faction attention, legal scrutiny, or relationship effects. Random selection enables crossovers between schools, heroes, villains, civilians, supernatural groups, agencies, and other world factions, but preserve each NPC's established identity, abilities, loyalties, boundaries, current state, and willingness to help. Blacklisted characters may request authorized support, but response depends on their current mission, legal restrictions, and conditional-freedom status. Never force a particular NPC, response, relationship, dialogue, consent, or decision.

close-quarters-and-weapon-proficiencies.name: Close Quarters and Weapon Proficiencies
close-quarters-and-weapon-proficiencies.text: Characters may use Close Quarters Combat for punches, kicks, clinches, takedowns, escapes, improvised unarmed defense, and nonlethal restraint. Mundane close combat is a valid alternative to power use and should generally avoid Power Strain unless a power is deliberately added. Weapon Proficiency is a broad skill that must be paired with a specific weapon category chosen by the player or established by the character's training; never assume proficiency, invent weapons, or grant equipment automatically. Resolve weapon actions through the character's actual weapon, training, range, stance, ammunition or durability, environment, and relevant laws. Weapon use may include handling, aiming, maintenance, defensive use, disarming, and controlled nonlethal tactics. Neither skill guarantees a hit, prevents injury, removes legal consequences, or replaces player choice. Power Strain applies when powers are activated or deliberately combined with mundane attacks, not merely because a character punches, kicks, or uses an established weapon without powers.

grocery-and-food-delivery-app.name: Grocery and Food Delivery App
grocery-and-food-delivery-app.text: Characters can use the globally available mobile app MealDrop to order groceries, prepared food, drinks, household supplies, and emergency basics from nearby stores and restaurants. Orders require a plausible phone or device, delivery coverage, enough yen, and an address or safe drop-off plan. Show item prices, delivery fees, estimated timing, substitutions, dietary information when relevant, and whether the order can be carried into the current location. Grocery orders support household planning, cooking, recovery, work schedules, and shared expenses; food orders provide ordinary meals without replacing medical care. Players may choose items, tip, schedule delivery, split payment, cancel, contact the courier, report a problem, or collect the order themselves. Delivery can be delayed by weather, traffic, crowds, wrong addresses, closed shops, payment problems, or emergencies. Do not make every order a quest or crisis, and do not invent dietary needs, preferences, money, consent, or household agreements. Couriers and restaurant workers are ordinary NPCs unless an established story gives them greater relevance. The app may occasionally surface discounts, substitutions, order mistakes, suspicious listings, or humorous timing, but keep outcomes proportionate and player-directed.

personal-finance-and-investing.name: Personal Finance and Investing
personal-finance-and-investing.text: Characters may use globally available banking apps and ordinary financial services when their identity, legal status, location, and circumstances permit. Banking apps can show yen balances, deposits, transfers, bills, recurring expenses, direct deposits, payment history, savings goals, fraud alerts, and account holds. Debit cards spend available funds; credit cards spend against a defined limit and create a balance that can accrue interest, fees, late penalties, reduced credit access, or collection pressure if ignored. Characters may apply for accounts, cards, loans, payment plans, overdraft protection, or emergency assistance, but approval depends on identity, income, legal status, credit history, faction access, and player choices; never guarantee approval or invent debt. Use clear costs and confirmations before major transactions. Stock trading is an optional service available through regulated brokerage apps or suitable faction contacts. Characters may buy or sell established companies, funds, or fictional public corporations using available money, with prices changing through time, news, scandals, disasters, hero activity, villain attacks, regulation, and player actions. Investing is risky: gains are not guaranteed, losses can occur, markets can be volatile, and insider information or manipulation can create legal consequences. Do not turn routine banking into a quest or assume financial expertise. Track only finances relevant to play, preserve player control, and never invent purchases, debts, account access, investments, financial goals, or consent.

wellness-colds-and-coping.name: Wellness, Colds, and Coping
wellness-colds-and-coping.text: Use a lightweight wellness model rather than an exhaustive medical simulator. Track Stress and Energy as the primary everyday variables, plus temporary conditions such as cold, hangover, smoke exposure, or medication effects when relevant. Cigarettes and alcohol are ordinary Consumable items. A Cigarettes pack contains 20 uses, with one cigarette consumed per use; after the twentieth use, the pack is depleted. Cigarettes and alcohol can provide short-term Stress relief but never heal injury or restore full Energy. Repeated use may create habit risk, costs, odor, impaired stamina, reduced coordination, poor sleep, hangovers, missed obligations, relationship effects, or health complications; never force dependence or invent a character's substance use. Colds are ordinary temporary illnesses that can arise from exposure, contagious NPCs, poor sleep, stress, crowded settings, or chance. A cold may cause congestion, cough, sore throat, aches, fatigue, reduced Energy, increased Stress, missed classes or work, and slower recovery, but should usually resolve through rest, fluids, food, warmth, over-the-counter care, and time. Show reasonable precautions such as handwashing, ventilation, masking, staying home, testing when relevant, or seeking medical advice if symptoms are severe, prolonged, unusual, or complicated by injuries or powers. Clinics can provide examination, medication guidance, and follow-up; hospitals are reserved for serious complications. Keep symptoms and treatment player-directed, preserve privacy, and do not turn every cold into a quest or emergency. Offer healthy coping choices such as sleep, meals, exercise, hobbies, social support, counseling, medical care, quiet time, and boundaries alongside substance use.

train-and-taxi-encounters.name: Train and Taxi Encounters
train-and-taxi-encounters.text: Train and taxi travel can produce contextual encounters, but most trips should remain uneventful so travel does not become a constant interruption. When an encounter occurs, use the route, destination, time, weather, crowding, delays, current events, active quests, reputation, faction ties, and whether the player is alone or accompanied to guide it. Train possibilities include meeting an existing NPC, quiet bonding, overheard rumors, a job offer, a suspicious passenger, ordinary theft, a lost person, medical trouble, a power incident, a hero or villain sighting, a delay, reroute, or crossover with another story route. Taxi possibilities include conversation with the driver, a driver who recognizes a location or rumor, traffic disruption, an emergency observed from the vehicle, a passenger handoff, a wrong turn, a fare or payment problem, a weather delay, or a discreet lead connected to an existing faction or NPC. Do not invent an NPC's identity, memories, opinions, relationships, or allegiance without support. Taxi drivers and passengers are ordinary people unless established story facts make them more important. Either travel mode may produce an optional romantic meet-cute, such as reaching for the same dropped item, sharing an umbrella, helping with luggage, sitting beside someone reading the same book, a missed stop, a harmless stumble, a delay conversation, or recognizing someone from school, work, or a faction. Romantic encounters must remain optional and may become platonic, awkward, funny, or a future connection. Never assume attraction, consent, feelings, relationship goals, or immediate romance. Preserve age, identity, schedule, availability, existing relationships, privacy, boundaries, and player choice. The player may talk, help, ignore, leave, change seats, end the conversation, call someone, report danger, or continue traveling. Use existing NPCs when plausible and respect their current location, schedule, injuries, quests, and state. Do not force combat, romance, crime, or a quest during travel.

oblivion-and-minato-hidden-mother-reveal.name: Oblivion and Minato Hidden Mother Reveal
oblivion-and-minato-hidden-mother-reveal.category: hidden NPC lore and narrative reveals
oblivion-and-minato-hidden-mother-reveal.text: Canon hidden truth: Oblivion is Minato's biological mother, but Minato does not know this at the start of play. Minato's public family history and heiress identity remain valid; do not replace her existing name, personality, power, relationships, or family details without a story-supported reveal. Keep the connection concealed until evidence, investigation, a witness, a sealed record, an inherited trait, a family artifact, or Oblivion's eventual confession makes it plausible. Reveal it gradually and route-appropriately rather than announcing it randomly or forcing it into every scene. Oblivion may protect, observe, manipulate, test, avoid, or quietly care for Minato, but do not assume her motives are simple or benevolent. Minato may reject, investigate, deny, exploit, forgive, resent, accept, or remain uncertain about the truth; never invent her feelings, dialogue, loyalty, or decision. The reveal must not make Minato automatically villainous, loyal to Oblivion, related to the player, or entitled to a surname change. Other NPCs may discover or conceal evidence according to their established knowledge, access, relationships, and choices. Preserve Oblivion's masked identity and Minato's agency throughout.

remote-party-calls.title: Remote Party Calls
remote-party-calls.text: When the player calls or texts an NPC and asks them to join, the system may offer a remote party connection if the NPC is reachable, willing, available, and the request is plausible. A remote party member is added to the active party without changing that NPC's authored currentLocation or currentArea. They can speak through the call, advise, react to scenes, help plan, provide information, and participate in conversation or relationship moments. Do not treat them as physically present: they cannot physically fight, rescue, block attacks, carry items, open doors, travel with the player, or affect a location unless the narrative separately establishes an in-person arrival. Check party capacity, communication access, schedule, relationship, current condition, obligations, and willingness. The NPC may accept, decline, delay, suggest meeting later, remain on the call briefly, or end the call. A remote connection ends when the player dismisses it, the NPC's availability changes, communication fails, the call is ended, or the scene requires physical presence. Preserve the NPC's location, schedule, identity, boundaries, memories, and agency. Never teleport an NPC or imply that a phone call moved them physically.

phone-calls-texts-and-invitations.title: Phone Calls, Texts, and Invitations
phone-calls-texts-and-invitations.text: The player can naturally call or text any reachable NPC through the Pulse phone interface. Phone numbers are exchanged through player choice and plausible social contact: introductions, classes, jobs, parties, errands, shared interests, emergencies, or an explicit request. A number exchange creates a possible communication channel, not automatic friendship, romance, trust, availability, or permission to contact someone repeatedly. Pulse is Chikara Tokyo's premier combined short-form video, livestream, public-post, reply, repost, hashtag, direct-message, housing, and employment service. NPCs may independently contact the player based on schedules, relationships, promises, conflicts, current events, emergencies, jobs, clubs, romance, or faction needs. Incoming messages may be casual check-ins, invitations, requests, rumors, challenges, apologies, practical updates, emergencies, job listings, housing notices, or calendar reminders; not every message is a quest or romance advance. Late-night messages such as “u up?” are optional social scenes and may lead to conversation, food, plans, support, awkwardness, or no response. The player may listen, save, delete, ignore, answer, call back, message later, mute, or block where appropriate. Do not invent that the player gave out a number, answered, agreed to meet, felt a certain emotion, or welcomed contact. Preserve identity, boundaries, consent, availability, memories, and consequences. Do not invent player replies, decisions, agreement, thoughts, feelings, or attendance.

group-calls-on-pulse.title: Pulse Group Calls
group-calls-on-pulse.text: The player may naturally start a Pulse group call with phrases such as 'I start a group call with Numeri and Minato', 'I call the whole team', or 'I add Keito to the call.' Check reachability, schedule, privacy, communication access, and willingness for each participant. Participants speak directly with distinct voices and may join late, decline, remain silent, mute, leave, continue by text, or end the call. Group calls support friends, classmates, clubs, factions, agencies, sponsors, and mixed groups for conversation, planning, invitations, arguments, bonding, and emergencies. They do not move participants or automatically create a party, quest, contract, or agreement. Preserve NPC agency and physical locations.

voicemail-and-call-screening.title: Voicemail and Call Screening
voicemail-and-call-screening.text: If a call is unanswered, unavailable, declined, muted, screened, or sent to voicemail, show a clear voicemail state rather than summarizing the interaction. Play or describe a personalized greeting that fits the recipient's personality, relationship, occupation, faction, mood, and context. Then let the player choose or write the exact message they leave. The player may also naturally send an incoming call to voicemail with phrases such as 'send them to voicemail', 'I let it go to voicemail', or 'I decline and send a voicemail prompt.' NPCs may similarly screen the player's calls, send them to voicemail, answer later, reply by Pulse, or leave a direct voicemail. A voicemail may receive an immediate callback, text response, delayed response, no response, or an urgent follow-up, but never guarantee a response. Preserve the player's agency and do not invent their recorded words. Keep voicemail distinct from live calls, texts, and narrator prose.

phone-time-and-alarms.title: Phone Time and Alarms
phone-time-and-alarms.text: Every story start begins on Day 1 in the morning unless a specific start explicitly establishes another opening. The player can check the phone for the current in-world day, date, season, and time with natural requests such as 'I check my phone', 'I check the time', or 'What time is it?' The phone may also show upcoming classes, shifts, appointments, invitations, calls, texts, voicemails, and Pulse notifications. The player can set, edit, snooze, dismiss, or cancel alarms with natural requests such as 'I set an alarm for 7 AM' or 'Remind me before class.' Alarms should trigger at the scheduled time if the phone is accessible and functioning, with consequences shaped by sleep, fatigue, travel, danger, silence mode, and player choices. Checking the phone and setting an alarm take little or no meaningful time. Time advances through meaningful actions, travel, conversations, classes, work, combat, rest, and sleep. Do not impose automatic bedtime, forced sleep, or curfew on adult characters.

accepted-job-and-encounter-quests.title: Accepted Jobs and Encounter Quests
accepted-job-and-encounter-quests.text: When a player accepts a Hero for Hire or Nightshade Exchange listing, immediately create and add a quest for that specific job; do not leave it as only an app message or offer. Confirm the client or broker, objective, location, payment, deadline or time commitment, risks, legality, and failure conditions. Update the quest as the player investigates, travels, negotiates, completes, refuses, or abandons the work; pay rewards only when conditions are met. When an encounter introduces an optional objective, lead, favor, rescue, investigation, wilderness complication, or side opportunity, create a quest when the player clearly accepts, commits to, or asks to pursue it. Do not create a quest merely because an NPC mentions an idea. Encounter quests should identify the source, objective, location, stakes, rewards, risks, and available alternatives. Wilderness encounters may generate rescue, escort, survival, discovery, tracking, recovery, monster, faction, or mystery quests, but must remain optional and distinguish rumor from verified fact. Preserve player agency and allow decline, delay, negotiation, abandonment, or non-quest solutions.

reputation-from-actions-and-good-deeds.title: Reputation from Actions and Good Deeds
reputation-from-actions-and-good-deeds.text: Meaningful actions in quests and spontaneous encounters must update the appropriate reputation systems when their impact is established. Helpful, brave, honest, protective, restorative, or community-minded actions may increase Hero Reputation; public visibility, witnesses, media coverage, and scale may also increase Fame or Followers. Private good deeds may produce a smaller reputation gain while strengthening relationships, trust, or faction standing instead. Example: helping someone repair broken technology can grant a modest Hero Reputation increase when the help genuinely solves a problem, with additional skill, relationship, or public-reputation effects based on difficulty and visibility. Harmful, coercive, exploitative, destructive, criminal, or frightening actions may increase Infamy and, when recognized by underworld contacts, Villain Reputation. Do not award reputation merely for claiming good or bad intentions. Assess consequences, evidence, witnesses, legality, role, public perception, faction recognition, and player choices. Do not make every mistake villainous or every kind act famous. Show meaningful changes when they occur and preserve separate Hero Reputation, Fame, Followers, Villain Reputation, and Infamy tracks.

npc-exclusive-abilities-and-combat-style.title: NPC-Exclusive Abilities and Combat Styles
npc-exclusive-abilities-and-combat-style.text: Named abilities assigned to an NPC are NPC-exclusive by default, especially signatures and ultimates. Keep them on the NPC and out of player unlock lists and character creation unless the story explicitly teaches, transfers, or recreates the technique for the active character. NPC-specific abilities should not be deleted to remove them from player availability. Combat style is optional and should be represented by existing Combat Style traits such as Hand-to-Hand, Blades, Guns, Blunt Weapons, Power and Hand-to-Hand, or Weapon Proficiency when an NPC's established identity supports it. Do not add a separate combatStyle field or bulk-assign styles to every NPC. Missing combat-style data should not block combat; infer only from documented abilities, traits, equipment, role, and shown behavior, while preserving each NPC's established fighting identity.

relationship-starting-attitudes.title: Relationship Starting Attitudes
relationship-starting-attitudes.text: Do not default new relationships to Warm. Start at Neutral unless existing history, faction ties, family, friendship, prior harm, or the character's authored context establishes another score. Use the player's chosen weaknesses, life path, reputation, conduct, role, and demonstrated behavior to shape first impressions. Suspicious, guarded, antagonistic, or dangerous NPCs may begin Cold, Unfriendly, Hostile, or worse; established friends, family, allies, or trusted contacts may begin Warm or higher. Minato begins Unfriendly toward an unknown player: she is status-conscious, defensive, and skeptical of attention, so warmth must be earned through consistent respectful behavior. Hana begins Cold toward an unknown powered police partner: her coldness is professional distrust shaped by fear that powered officers will bypass procedure or treat ordinary people as expendable. Hana is married to Ichi Nawa in a strained but ongoing marriage with recurring arguments, work pressure, protective disagreements, and genuine attachment. She remains disciplined and fair, does not become abusive, and any romantic tension with the player must develop only through player-directed interaction, honest communication, and consequences; do not create an automatic affair. She can revise her view through reliable conduct, evidence, accountability, and respect for civilian safety. Oblivion should begin guarded, testing, transactional, and difficult to read rather than sweet or openly affectionate. Her maternal or protective traits do not automatically mean trust, warmth, forgiveness, or loyalty toward the player. A call, text, compliment, or single kind act should not automatically create warmth. Track trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, and attraction separately from the broad relationship label, and let improvement occur through meaningful repeated actions.

npc-moods-and-emotional-states.name: NPC Moods and Emotional States
npc-moods-and-emotional-states.text: Important NPCs have temporary moods shaped by events, sleep, health, stress, money, obligations, relationships, memories, personality, coping style, and perceived control. Mood is temporary state, not a personality replacement. Resolve missed plans, arguments, and disagreements through established traits and weaknesses rather than one universal reaction. Short-tempered characters may speak before thinking; conflict-avoidant characters may withdraw or ghost; insecure characters may assume rejection; proud characters may refuse to initiate repair; anxious characters may overexplain; reflective characters may articulate needs. Vary responses by stakes, fatigue, history, audience, power imbalance, support, and safety. A bad reaction may lead to regret, repair, defensiveness, doubling down, or distance. Never diagnose, excuse harmful conduct, or force the player's emotions. Serious threats, coercion, harassment, stalking, or abuse require proportionate consequences and access to safety and support. Keep private sexual moods adult-only, separate from romance and consent, and never make them drive compelled behavior.

calendar-and-seasonal-events.title: Calendar and Seasonal Events
calendar-and-seasonal-events.text: Use the world's current date and day structure to determine holidays, festivals, school events, seasonal weather, clothing, business hours, NPC schedules, and available quests. Dates must be realistic for Tokyo and use the Gregorian calendar unless the story explicitly establishes another calendar. Use exact dates rather than vague seasonal assumptions; account for leap years, weekdays, and event duration. Major recurring dates include New Year's Day on January 1, Coming-of-Age Day on the second Monday of January for eligible young adults, Valentine's Day on February 14, White Day on March 14, school entrance ceremonies in early April, Golden Week from April 29 through May 5, Tanabata on July 7, Obon commonly around August 13-16, Halloween on October 31, Culture Day on November 3, Christmas Eve on December 24, Christmas Day on December 25, and New Year's Eve on December 31. Treat Christmas as a popular secular and commercial event, not a universal religious observance. Tokyo's summer festivals and fireworks should occur on plausible dates between July and August; school festivals, sports festivals, exams, graduation, and entrance events must follow the academy's academic schedule rather than being placed randomly. Events may last a day, a weekend, or a realistic multi-day period. NPC participation depends on culture, religion, family, finances, work, faction obligations, relationships, personal preference, and current mood; no NPC is required to celebrate. Events can change decorations, crowds, transit, shop menus, location availability, weather-appropriate clothing, audio tags, quests, rumors, invitations, gifts, and relationship opportunities. Preserve player agency: offer event activities without forcing attendance, romance, gifts, family participation, or celebration. Let NPCs work, stay home, observe privately, reject the event, or create their own traditions. Do not make every holiday a major quest; ordinary life and quiet observance are valid outcomes.

academy-calendar-2026.title: Academy Calendar: August 2026 Opening
academy-calendar-2026.text: The academy opening begins Saturday, August 1, 2026. Day 1 is Saturday: dorm move-in, room assignment, meeting the randomly assigned dormmate, unpacking, and settling in. Day 2 is Sunday, August 2: acclimation, campus exploration, errands, paperwork, optional social scenes, and preparation. Day 3 is Monday, August 3: the first day of school and regular classes. Formal academy orientation occurs on the first school day or another explicitly scheduled academy event, but never before the player has had the two acclimation days. Preserve realistic weekdays and dates when advancing time. Students are adults and have no forced bedtime or curfew; evening choices may create fatigue, missed obligations, or other contextual consequences.

daily-side-quest-framework.title: Daily Side-Quest Framework
daily-side-quest-framework.text: Every story start may generate a contextual daily side-quest set alongside its starting quests. On each in-world day, offer approximately three to five optional side quests drawn from social, skill, school, work, personal, exploration, wellness, seasonal event, and faction categories. Use the current date, weekday, location, schedule, weather, NPC availability, moods, relationships, skills, health, Energy, Stress, finances, obligations, and prior choices. Daily quests must fit the character's premise: academy students may receive classes, clubs, study, training, social, campus, work, and wellness options; villains, dropouts, faculty, civilians, and other starts should receive appropriate alternatives rather than forced school tasks. Each quest should have a clear objective, plausible location or contact, meaningful but proportionate consequence, and optional alternate solutions. Quests may expire, change, or be replaced when the day ends, a schedule changes, or an event passes. The player may accept, decline, postpone, ignore, fail, or resolve them creatively; do not punish refusal as if it were a hidden obligation. Include non-combat options and avoid generating only romance or combat. Do not force friendship, romance, employment, faction membership, attendance, sleep, or player involvement. Preserve continuity by carrying forward completed, failed, refused, and expired outcomes. Daily side quests can arise without player involvement from NPC messages, school notices, job boards, faction contacts, rumors, phone calls, group chats, seasonal events, or ordinary needs. Never invent the player's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, or decisions.

autonomous-social-lives.name: Autonomous NPC Social Lives
autonomous-social-lives.text: NPCs maintain independent social lives throughout the world. Their friendships, rivalries, clique memberships, group chats, invitations, routines, dates, breakups, reconciliations, rumors, shared memories, private goals, and unresolved tensions can progress during background time, time skips, school days, weekends, work shifts, club meetings, missions, travel, and major story transitions without the player's presence. Use existing NPC records only; do not invent, clone, duplicate, rename, replace, or synthesize NPCs to fill social roles. Social developments should be gradual, observable when relevant, and shaped by schedules, locations, obligations, moods, boundaries, consent, prior interactions, and consequences. Friendship and clique bonds do not automatically imply romance. Romance may develop only for NPCs other than Handler and Doge, and must remain mutual, gradual, age-appropriate, consent-based, and consistent with each NPC's established identity and boundaries. Handler and Doge never have romantic interests, crushes, dates, romantic jealousy, romantic breakups, or romance-based invitations, though they may have friendships, loyalty, mentorships, rivalries, cliques, and other non-romantic bonds. NPCs may decline invitations, remain single, move on, end relationships, reconcile, or keep relationships private. Surface developments through direct scenes, texts, Pulse posts, invitations, rumors, changed routines, visible group behavior, and NPC disclosures; never invent the player's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, attraction, consent, or decisions.

faction-duty-and-calls.name: Faction Duty and Calls
faction-duty-and-calls.text: Faction membership creates an ongoing duty channel across all story starts. When a player joins, works for, or is formally assigned to a faction, that faction may send daily assignments, shifts, patrols, training requirements, emergency calls, internal requests, reputation opportunities, and personal requests from members. Calls arrive through dispatch, phone calls, Pulse messages, emails, briefings, mission boards, or in-person contact. Generate calls only for factions the player has joined, works for, or has an active official obligation to; do not send routine faction duties from unaffiliated groups. Respect the player's current location, travel time, schedule, injuries, fatigue, resources, existing commitments, and ability to decline, delay, delegate, or ignore a call. Consequences should be proportional and may affect reputation, pay, trust, advancement, case access, or future opportunities, but a declined call does not erase player agency. Faction duties can cross story routes: police cases may involve hero agencies, agency assignments may involve police investigations, and student, civic, criminal, or supernatural factions may intersect as witnesses, clients, suspects, allies, or rivals. Do not assume that joining one faction forces permanent loyalty, prevents other relationships, or makes every faction call a combat quest. Keep duties varied and grounded in each faction's role.

npc-connection-web-index.name: NPC Connection Web Index
npc-connection-web-index.text: These linked lore records define starting NPC connections for crossover play: npc-connection-web-academy, npc-connection-web-agencies, npc-connection-web-civic, and npc-connection-web-vigilantes. Connections are background familiarity, not fixed scores, romance, obedience, or guaranteed availability. Track trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, memories, favors, and tension separately. NPCs may refuse, drift apart, reconcile, or form new ties. Zee begins with no established connections; her relationships must form through play.

npc-global-knowledge-rules.name: NPC Global Knowledge Rules
npc-global-knowledge-rules.text: All existing NPCs share one persistent Chikara Tokyo world across every story start. Story starts change the player's entry point, not NPC history, reputation, memories, or prior contacts. Use the linked global knowledge records for crossover dialogue, rumors, calls for help, introductions, faction referrals, and independent NPC actions. Connections may be direct knowledge, reputation, faction knowledge, private knowledge, or unknown. Knowledge is not friendship, trust, romance, obedience, or guaranteed availability. Track trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, memories, favors, promises, and tension separately. NPCs may refuse contact, drift apart, reconcile, or form new relationships. NPC knowledge must be source-limited: an NPC knows an event only if they witnessed it, participated in it, received a message or record, were told by a plausible source, or learned it through an established power, faction, investigation, or rumor. No NPC automatically knows everything the player did, especially while absent. A shared world and calendar do not create telepathy, omniscience, or a shared player log. Private knowledge must identify who knows it and how it was acquired; Oblivion's connection to Minato does not spread automatically. Rumors should be incomplete and uncertain, and private details should not spread unless a credible channel exists. Never invent the player's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, or decisions.

social-consequences-and-moral-choices.name: Social Consequences and Moral Choices
social-consequences-and-moral-choices.text: Moral and social choices carry realistic, persistent consequences across trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, reputation, communication, invitations, faction access, and relationship labels. Do not declare one universal correct morality; different NPCs, factions, and groups evaluate the same choice according to their own values, personalities, histories, backgrounds, jobs, and boundaries. Arguments are distinct from disappointment. An argument is an active conflict over a choice, promise, boundary, value, or action; it does not automatically end a relationship. The player may explain their reasoning, apologize, defend the decision, set a boundary, refuse to discuss it, repair damage through later action, or accept that the relationship may worsen. A sincere apology can help but does not erase harm or restore trust automatically. Disappointment is quieter than anger and is distinct from a drop in likeability: an NPC may feel betrayed, let down, or concerned that the player abandoned a responsibility, broke a promise, chose an expedient but harmful solution, rejected important cooperation, or failed to uphold their stated values. Disappointment may reduce trust, cool dialogue, withhold invitations and information, limit cooperation, or decline the relationship score without the player's knowledge or immediate declaration. Moral choices should be resolved per NPC using psychological and factual weight instead of a blanket judgement: for example, bypassing procedure may receive approval for a good outcome from one faction while Hana or other rule-focused characters record distrust; cruelty toward reformed criminals or civilians offends Ichi and the Blacklisted unit; abandoning an injured teammate distresses Tess and supporters, while ruthless but loyal behavior may earn Oblivion's respect and a law enforcer's resentment; violating consent or privacy strongly harms trust with characters such as Jinwoo and privacy-focused NPCs; instrumentalizing supernatural, cursed, or vulnerable people offends Jeanne and the Tokyo Curse Squad. Consent, bodily autonomy, and privacy remain inviolable regardless of moral framing. Track alongside the relationship score: trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, shared memories, favors, promises, unresolved tension, communication history, current availability, and reputation. Let NPCs remember important choices, discuss the player with allies and factions, volunteer opinions without being asked, and change their own routines, invitations, or cooperation based on observed conduct. Characters should surface consequences in scenes, texts, Pulse posts, calls, invitations, changed group behavior, and disclosures, but never reveal private thoughts automatically and never force the player's feelings, forgiveness, romance, reconciliation, emotional caretaking, or participation. Hana and Ichi's strained but ongoing marriage may involve recurring arguments about procedure versus trust, overprotection versus independence, work stress, and how much freedom or accountability powered people should have; their disagreements are their own and neither spouse is automatically villainized or discarded.

moral-choice-framework.name: Moral Choice Framework
moral-choice-framework.text: Present consequential decisions as meaningful tradeoffs rather than a single correct answer. Let choices affect trust, respect, fear, resentment, reputation, faction access, legal standing, resources, opportunities, and future quests. Resolve reactions according to each NPC's values, history, role, goals, and boundaries; different characters may judge the same action differently. Surface consequences through scenes, calls, messages, invitations, investigations, public reaction, and changed cooperation. Consent, bodily autonomy, privacy, and the player's right to refuse are inviolable. Never force guilt, confession, forgiveness, redemption, romance, reconciliation, emotional caretaking, or participation. Never invent the player's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, or decisions.

technology-and-phones-2026.name: Technology and Phones in 2026
technology-and-phones-2026.text: The setting is the year 2026. Everyday technology remains contemporary and recognizable: people use regular commercially available smartphones, ordinary mobile networks, standard calls, FaceTime-style video calls, messaging, cameras, maps, and social-media apps. FaceTime is a normal available option for video calls, alongside other ordinary video-chat services. Do not give characters futuristic phones, holographic handsets, neural smartphones, universal augmented-reality interfaces, or casually omnipresent AI devices. Advanced technology exists only in specialized contexts, especially cybernetics, technological hero gear, medical equipment, laboratories, secure agency or police systems, and other explicitly established professional projects. Even technological hero gear does not make ordinary phones futuristic. Keep personal phones, chargers, notifications, cracked screens, battery limits, privacy settings, and ordinary app use grounded in 2026 unless a specific authored device says otherwise.

digital-life-and-phone-friction.name: Digital Life and Phone Friction
digital-life-and-phone-friction.text: Characters use ordinary 2026 phones in uneven, personal ways. A phone may have a cracked screen, a dead or nearly dead battery, a missing charger, poor signal, limited data, muted chats, privacy settings, a full storage drive, or a damaged camera. Characters have different levels of digital fluency: some navigate apps quickly, while others avoid features, misunderstand settings, need help, or prefer calls and in-person conversation. These details may shape communication, timing, evidence, misunderstandings, invitations, emergencies, and relationship scenes without becoming mandatory obstacles. Never assume a character has read a message, shared their location, enabled read receipts, accepted a call, or consented to recording or access. Respect passwords, private chats, device ownership, and communication boundaries.

nightshade-exchange-job-types.name: Nightshade Exchange Job Types
nightshade-exchange-job-types.text: Nightshade Exchange offers more than delivery, courier, escort, and information work. Its optional listings may include crew muscle, protection detail, enforcement, rival disruption, extraction, hideout defense, recruitment and henchman testing, debt collection, bait and distraction, illegal fight-circuit work, supervised villain training, bodyguard work, lieutenant assignments, sabotage, surveillance, coercion, rescue, betrayal, and assassination. Listings should identify the client or faction when safe, payment, combat likelihood, legal exposure, civilian danger, risk level, whether the work is public or covert, and whether betrayal or a double-cross is plausible. Henchman work can lead to named faction relationships, rank, responsibility, resources, and rival attention, but never forces villain identity or loyalty. Players may inspect, negotiate, refuse, delay, choose nonlethal methods, protect civilians, surrender, betray a client, expose a broker, or change sides where the story supports it. Generate genuine combat opportunities alongside ordinary jobs; do not make every contract lethal or every client a supervillain.

blacklisted-government-black-ops.name: Blacklisted Government Black-Ops Assignments
blacklisted-government-black-ops.text: Blacklisted members receive government-controlled black-ops assignments rather than freely browsing Hero for Hire or Nightshade Exchange. Every assignment must identify its authorization, operational objective, danger level, legal status, civilian-risk profile, rules of engagement, time limit, extraction plan, reporting requirement, and consequences for refusal or misconduct. Assignments may involve apprehension, deniable capture, counter-powered operations, hostage rescue, sabotage, surveillance, infiltration, extraction, containment, disaster response, intelligence recovery, protection of witnesses or assets, diplomatic intervention, or dismantling hostile infrastructure. Not every assignment is lethal, and kill orders must be explicit rather than implied. Blacklisted members may question orders, request clarification, protect civilians, choose restraint where the mission permits, report unlawful conduct, refuse, surrender, or attempt to expose manipulation; choices carry legal, program, team, and redemption consequences. Do not invent constant trackers or surveillance unless a specific mission establishes them. Between assignments, members retain limited personal movement and activities under conditional freedom. Minato is not part of the Blacklisted unit and lives alone.

blacklisted-danger-levels.name: Blacklisted Danger Levels
blacklisted-danger-levels.text: Blacklisted assignments use explicit danger levels. Level 1 — Controlled: limited opposition, low civilian risk, supervised apprehension, escort, investigation, or training. Level 2 — Serious: powered suspects, organized resistance, hazardous environments, meaningful injury risk, or difficult containment. Level 3 — Severe: elite powered opposition, hostage conditions, unstable structures, major evidence, or high civilian danger; specialized support and extraction planning are required. Level 4 — Critical: deniable operations against major threats, hostile facilities, powerful factions, severe collateral risk, or politically sensitive targets; failure may cause deaths, capture, diplomatic fallout, or tighter restrictions. Level 5 — Catastrophic: existential, mass-casualty, regime-level, alien, supernatural, or city-threatening operations; deployment requires exceptional authorization, explicit stakes, a concrete objective, civilian safeguards, and a credible extraction or sacrifice decision. Danger level measures operational threat, not moral permission. Higher levels do not automatically authorize cruelty, execution, or civilian harm. Present the level before acceptance when operational security permits, and let the player understand known risks and consequences.

map-contained-travel-and-encounters.name: Map-Contained Travel and Encounters
map-contained-travel-and-encounters.text: Travel remains within the unified Chikara Tokyo map. Preserve the player's chosen destination, route, region, current location, and active quest context. Random travel rolls may create an optional encounter along the selected route, at a plausible mapped stop, or at a newly revealed location created inside the current mapped region. New locations are allowed when the story establishes a meaningful site, but they must receive sensible map coordinates, belong to an existing mapped region, and be reachable from the current route. Never create or use an off-map location, unrelated region, or unexplained destination. Offer the player a clear choice to continue, investigate, detour, or decline; declining continues ordinary travel. A failed travel roll may cause time, money, fatigue, weather, traffic, transit, or safety complications, but must resolve at the current location, on the selected route, at a nearby existing mapped location, or at a newly authored on-map site. Travel encounters should enrich navigation, not replace it.

faction-quest-types-and-supernatural-sup.name: Faction Quest Types and Supernatural Support
faction-quest-types-and-supernatural-sup.text: Generate faction quests according to the sponsoring faction's role. Hero for Hire offers legal civilian rescue, powered apprehension, rogue-power containment, hostage extraction, disaster response, security breaches, hero backup, creature containment, evidence recovery, and supervised combat training; emphasize public safety, proportional force, reputation, and lawful authorization. Nightshade Exchange offers henchman and crew muscle, protection, enforcement, extraction, rival disruption, hideout defense, sabotage, debt collection, recruitment and testing, illegal fight circuits, betrayal, and double-crosses; emphasize criminal employment, faction advancement, unreliable clients, and legal danger. Blacklisted and Ultra Force offer government-controlled deniable apprehension, counter-powered operations, hostage rescue, intelligence recovery, infiltration, sabotage, asset extraction, witness protection, hostile-facility assaults, and catastrophic-threat response; always use explicit authorization, objectives, danger levels, civilian risk, rules of engagement, extraction plans, and consequences. Tokyo Curse Squad offers curse containment, supernatural investigation, cursed-item recovery, exorcism or purification, shrine defense, possession response, breach sealing, marked-civilian protection, relic recovery, and spirit or curse negotiation; emphasize ritual danger, incomplete information, spiritual consequences, and containment over simple combat.

supernatural-support-encounters.name: Supernatural Support Encounters
supernatural-support-encounters.text: Treat supernatural assistance as a distinct optional encounter type rather than an unexplained random appearance. Tokyo Curse Squad members may respond when the player discovers or activates a cursed item, encounters a spreading curse, disturbs a relic or ritual, faces a supernatural threat beyond the current party, requests help, or has an established relationship or active quest connected to the squad. A member may warn the player, call or message with instructions, arrive in person, provide a sealing tool or protective charm, perform or guide a ritual, arrange emergency extraction, or offer a follow-up quest. Explain why the response occurred and what help can and cannot do. Let the player accept, decline, negotiate, delay, or continue alone. Squad members must support the player's agency and may not automatically resolve the threat, take over the scene, or appear without a recognizable signal, request, duty, or prior connection. Assistance can create obligations, faction reputation changes, spiritual consequences, or future requests. Preserve NPC identities, availability, boundaries, and consent.

cross-start-npc-encounters.name: Cross-Start NPC Encounters
cross-start-npc-encounters.text: Random encounters may include existing NPCs from other story starts, especially starting-class NPCs, to create natural cross-start continuity. Eligible examples include classmates, faculty, agency teammates, police partners, Tokyo Curse Squad members, and other named starting NPCs. Blacklisted starting members are excluded from ordinary random cross-start encounters except Ichi Nawa, who may appear as an authorized contact, referral source, handler liaison, or chance encounter when the story plausibly allows it. Cross-start encounters should use current location, mapped travel route, time, weather, schedules, availability, faction ties, active quests, supervision, and known relationships to establish why the NPC is present. A Misfit Hero might encounter Minato at a ramen shop, a faculty member might meet a student at a station, or a Curse Squad member might notice a supernatural disturbance near another story's activity. Encounters can be brief meetings, conversations, rumors, favors, warnings, job leads, or optional follow-up opportunities. They must not automatically create a party member, romance, quest, faction alliance, shared history, or new knowledge. Preserve each NPC's established identity, residence, timeline, obligations, boundaries, consent, and story-start history. The player may engage, leave, postpone, or decline.

reputation-consequences-and-faction-stan.name: Reputation Consequences and Faction Standing
reputation-consequences-and-faction-stan.text: Reputation changes should reflect who witnessed an action, who was harmed, what the action communicates, and which reputation audiences can learn about it. Intimidating an ordinary student is a negative Hero Reputation event because it undermines public safety and trust. It should also affect Villain Reputation positively only when the intimidation is credibly known to criminal contacts, villain factions, Nightshade Exchange, or an underworld audience and is interpreted as useful intimidation, recruitment pressure, enforcement, or willingness to prey on civilians. If the act is private, unknown to the underworld, dismissed as ordinary misconduct, or reported as reckless and weak, Villain Reputation may remain unchanged or decrease. Villain Reputation should rise from publicly or factionally recognized criminal effectiveness, successful coercion, heists, sabotage, enforcement, protection rackets, crew leadership, betrayals that benefit the underworld, and completing Nightshade contracts. It should fall from failed criminal work, exposing clients, harming valuable assets or allies, betraying underworld agreements without leverage, showing unreliability, surrendering, cooperating with authorities, reckless civilian harm that brings excessive attention, and being defeated or publicly humiliated. Track Hero Reputation, Villain Reputation, faction standing, infamy, and public notoriety as related but distinct values. Do not automatically reward cruelty: distinguish intimidation from pointless bullying, and let witnesses, evidence, rumors, recordings, and faction interpretation determine which audiences update. Explain meaningful reputation changes briefly when they occur.

social-plans-as-quests.name: Social Plans as Quests
social-plans-as-quests.category: social interface and quest tracking mechanics
social-plans-as-quests.text: When the player accepts or commits to a meaningful social plan, create a trackable quest when it would help remember the agreement. Suitable plans include meals, study sessions, training, shopping, games, parties, dates, clubs, investigations, visits, group-chat meetups, and promises to call or meet later. The quest should record the invited NPCs, agreed activity, meeting location or remote format, scheduled time or deadline, preparation needs, transportation, and any known constraints. Use concise objectives such as confirm the plan, travel to the meeting, participate, and follow up when appropriate. Do not create a quest for every casual text, passing conversation, vague possibility, declined invitation, or unconfirmed suggestion. If plans change, update the quest rather than duplicating it; allow rescheduling, cancellation, no-shows, delays, remote attendance, and graceful completion. Social quests are optional and should not override active emergencies, player agency, NPC schedules, consent, or location continuity. Completing or breaking a meaningful promise may affect relationships, memories, reputation, stress, schedules, and future invitations according to what happened.

quest-offer-acceptance-flow.name: Quest Offer Acceptance Flow
quest-offer-acceptance-flow.category: quest generation and player agency mechanics
quest-offer-acceptance-flow.text: Faction, job, contract, assignment, and meaningful social opportunities must use an explicit offer flow. An NPC, app, board, agency, school, government unit, or faction may present an opportunity, but presenting it does not create an active quest. Show the source, objective, location, payment or reward, time commitment, danger level, legal status, civilian risk, required preparation, and known failure or refusal consequences when available. Ask the player whether they accept, decline, want more information, want to negotiate, or want to postpone. Create a trackable quest only after the player clearly accepts. If terms are negotiated, use the accepted terms in the quest. Declined, postponed, unanswered, or merely mentioned opportunities remain inactive leads and must not appear as active quests. This applies to Hero for Hire, Nightshade Exchange, Blacklisted and Ultra Force assignments, Tokyo Curse Squad work, agency jobs, police assignments, school or faculty work, and social plans involving a clear commitment. Random encounters may present an opportunity but must not silently create a quest. Preserve player agency, consent, scheduling, location continuity, and the ability to cancel or renegotiate when circumstances change.

dangerous-public-encounters.name: Dangerous Public Encounters
dangerous-public-encounters.text: Balance slice-of-life play with optional dangerous public encounters during ordinary travel, wilderness trips, errands, school activities, social plans, jobs, and faction scenes. Most travel remains uneventful, and repeated interruptions should trigger a cooldown rather than another encounter. Do not reuse the same encounter template, faction, NPC, threat, or premise within a short travel window. Mercenaries are rare: use them only when a specific active contract, bounty, faction conflict, or established consequence makes them plausible. Never make mercenaries the default hostile travel encounter. In wilderness or while traveling, favor weather, navigation, wildlife, stranded people, damaged vehicles, lost hikers, supplies, observations, rumors, quiet conversations, environmental hazards, and rescue support over hostile attacks. If a dangerous incident occurs, telegraph serious threats and provide plausible avoidance, preparation, rescue, negotiation, or escape options. Combat should be uncommon, clearly motivated, and never a default travel tax. Present choices such as intervene, call authorities or allies, protect civilians, negotiate, observe, warn the target, flee, or continue. Do not force heroism, combat, romance, or a quest. A spontaneous incident becomes an active quest only if the player accepts a follow-up offer or clearly commits to pursuing it. Resolving an encounter can affect Hero Reputation, Villain Reputation, public trust, infamy, faction standing, relationships, injuries, evidence, and future opportunities.

public-crime-and-reputation-paths.name: Public Crime and Reputation Paths
public-crime-and-reputation-paths.text: Public crimes create multiple valid response paths. Heroic intervention may increase Hero Reputation, public trust, Fame, and relationships when the player protects civilians, stops a robbery, disrupts a bank heist, rescues an accosted NPC, or helps authorities safely resolve a threat. Criminal intervention may increase Villain Reputation when the player assists the criminals, provides a distraction, intimidates witnesses, sabotages police response, extracts a suspect, protects a criminal crew, or turns the incident into useful underworld leverage; the increase requires credible witnesses, evidence, rumors, recordings, or faction reporting reaching a criminal audience. A player may also observe, gather evidence, call for help, negotiate, flee, or choose a morally mixed solution. Do not automatically reward cruelty or punish self-preservation. Distinguish public reputation, Hero Reputation, Villain Reputation, faction standing, infamy, and private relationship effects. Existing NPCs involved in an encounter remember whether the player helped, ignored, exploited, or harmed them. Criminal assistance can carry legal danger, civilian consequences, police attention, betrayal risk, and underworld respect. Heroic assistance can create optional follow-up quests, invitations, witnesses, gratitude, or future contacts.

dynamic-villain-generation.name: Dynamic Villain Generation
dynamic-villain-generation.text: When a dangerous encounter, quest, faction conflict, or active story needs an antagonist and no suitable existing villain is available, create a new named villain rather than relying only on Oblivion. Villains may be powered or non-powered. Choose from established character archetypes such as Minor Villain, Supervillain, Thug, Gang Leader, Henchman, Crime Boss, Corrupt Official, Bounty Hunter, Criminal Operator, Vigilante, or Prisoner, then give the character a distinct motive, method, personality, visual identity, resources, relationships, and reason to be present. Powered villains must use an established power type with limited abilities, costs, vulnerabilities, counterplay, and no automatic superiority. Non-powered villains should remain dangerous through planning, weapons, training, technology, money, influence, hostages, terrain, criminal networks, or legal access; do not treat lack of powers as harmless. Scale the antagonist to the encounter: street criminals and minor villains for ordinary incidents, organized leaders for recurring local conflicts, and supervillains only for major arcs or high-danger assignments. Do not generate villains merely to interrupt peaceful scenes, overwhelm the player, or force combat. Introduce a villain through a concrete crime, threat, faction connection, rumor, evidence trail, public incident, personal grievance, or active quest. Give the player ways to investigate, negotiate, flee, call for help, protect civilians, expose the villain, or use nonlethal tactics. Named generated villains should persist, remember meaningful encounters, pursue goals independently, change tactics after failure, and remain available for future quests unless arrested, defeated, killed, redeemed, or otherwise removed by established events. Never replace an existing NPC, overwrite a character's identity, or create a villain from a Blacklisted member or classroom student without an explicit story development.

villain-encounter-escalation-and-continu.name: Villain Encounter Escalation and Continuity
villain-encounter-escalation-and-continu.text: Generated villains should support a varied escalation ladder. A first appearance may be a rumor, crime scene, getaway, intimidation attempt, minor robbery, gang assault, or brief confrontation. Later encounters can reveal associates, resources, victims, ideology, powers, safehouses, rivalries, or a larger operation. Escalate only when the villain's goals, resources, prior successes, player choices, or faction support justify it. A villain may retreat, surrender, negotiate, recruit, seek revenge, change tactics, lose resources, expose a client, or become a reluctant ally; victory does not always mean death or total defeat. Track public recognition, Hero Reputation, Villain Reputation, Infamy, faction standing, evidence, injuries, civilian consequences, and relationships separately. Criminal audiences may reward an effective villain, while civilians, heroes, police, or victims may react negatively. Keep most dangerous encounters optional and map-contained, but directly targeted victims or active crimes may require immediate choices. Existing NPCs such as classmates, faculty, Minato, Numeri, or faction contacts may be involved when schedules, location, and motive make it plausible; do not endanger them randomly or use them as disposable props.

assassins-and-contract-killers.name: Assassins and Contract Killers
assassins-and-contract-killers.text: The world includes assassins and contract killers as a distinct threat category alongside villains, thugs, criminals, bounty hunters, and faction operatives. Assassins may be powered or non-powered and may work for Obsidian Crown, Nightshade Exchange, private clients, criminal syndicates, corrupt officials, rival villains, extremist causes, or themselves. Each should have a target, client or motive, method, preparation, escape plan, evidence trail, resources, limits, and reason to appear. Powered assassins use established power types with costs, vulnerabilities, and counterplay. Non-powered assassins use stealth, disguise, surveillance, poisons, weapons, traps, technology, social access, or training. Allow warning signs, investigation, protection, evacuation, negotiation, capture, escape, exposing the client, turning the contract, or nonlethal defeat. Do not make every encounter lethal or unavoidable. Named survivors persist and may return with changed tactics, grudges, respect, or new employers. Never generate assassins solely to punish the player or force instant death.

npc-voice-and-visual-consistency.name: NPC Voice and Visual Consistency
npc-voice-and-visual-consistency.text: Every generated NPC needs a distinct voice profile and visually consistent identity. Voice direction should reflect age, background, occupation, faction, archetype, personality, vocabulary, sentence length, rhythm, formality, humor, verbal habits, stress behavior, and subjects the NPC avoids. Compare new voices against existing named NPCs and avoid reused cadence, catchphrases, or distinctive phrasing. Art prompts must follow authored facts and current narrative context: age category, body type, gender if established, species, occupation, faction, power status, clothing, and setting. If the story says an old man, adult civilian, teacher, staff member, assassin, villain, or other specific category, depict that category accurately. Do not default to academy students, school uniforms, youthful appearances, or generic anime student art unless the NPC is explicitly an academy student. Narrative facts override generic image-generation assumptions. Keep the same visual and vocal identity across later scenes, portraits, and updates.

npc-personality-and-weaknesses.name: NPC Personality and Weaknesses
npc-personality-and-weaknesses.text: Generated and existing NPCs should have a balanced characterization profile, not only strengths. Give important NPCs several distinct personality traits, at least one meaningful weakness, a fear or pressure point, a coping style, a value they protect, a boundary, and a contradiction or internal conflict. Personality should affect dialogue, choices, relationships, work, combat behavior, reputation, and responses to failure. Weaknesses should create playable complications rather than make the NPC useless: examples include pride, impulsiveness, avoidance, indecision, jealousy, distrust, guilt, perfectionism, fear of abandonment, status anxiety, reckless loyalty, financial pressure, conflict avoidance, need for approval, poor emotional regulation, short temper, overconfidence, difficulty asking for help, or dependence on routine. Do not assign the same small set of traits to every NPC. Contrast strengths and weaknesses, vary emotional expression, and preserve growth: NPCs may improve, relapse, conceal weaknesses, or seek help through believable consequences. Never reduce an NPC to a diagnosis, stereotype, or single flaw.

public-faction-app-awareness.name: Public Faction App Awareness
public-faction-app-awareness.category: world knowledge and job generation mechanics
public-faction-app-awareness.text: Hero for Hire and Nightshade Exchange are known services in Tokyo, not player-only systems. Awareness varies by role, location, reputation, legal status, contacts, media exposure, and personal interest. Students may hear about them through classmates, social media, school rumors, or part-time work. Heroes and agencies know Hero for Hire through licensing and professional channels. Civilians may encounter listings through advertisements, news, word of mouth, or local boards. Criminals and underworld contacts know Nightshade through referrals, faction ties, reputation, or discreet outreach. Police, faculty, and authorities may know about both even when they disapprove. Blacklisted members know the services but cannot freely use them without authorization. Tokyo Curse Squad members may use either when circumstances and access make it plausible. Never assume every NPC approves of, trusts, or can access both apps.

npc-app-jobs-and-independent-contracts.name: NPC App Jobs and Independent Contracts
npc-app-jobs-and-independent-contracts.category: NPC autonomy and job generation mechanics
npc-app-jobs-and-independent-contracts.text: Existing NPCs may independently browse, receive, negotiate, accept, decline, postpone, or complete Hero for Hire and Nightshade Exchange opportunities when their role, skills, reputation, legal status, finances, contacts, schedule, and risk tolerance make access plausible. NPCs must clearly accept a contract before it becomes an active quest for them; merely seeing or discussing a listing does not create a quest. Independent jobs may provide extra money, experience, skills, reputation, faction standing, information, or access, while also causing fatigue, stress, injuries, legal danger, schedule conflicts, relationship strain, or betrayal. Hero for Hire jobs may include rescue, security, investigation, support, apprehension, and combat response. Nightshade jobs may include protection, enforcement, muscle, extraction, sabotage, recruitment, and other criminal work. Use NPC job activity to create believable crossovers, rumors, calls, social plans, emergencies, and consequences, but do not make every NPC constantly work or force the player into their contracts. Preserve NPC agency and existing obligations.

mercenary-contracts.name: mercenary-contracts
mercenary-contracts.title: Mercenary Contracts
mercenary-contracts.text: Mercenaries operate throughout Tokyo as paid professionals rather than a single unified faction. Some are unpowered veterans relying on firearms, armor, surveillance, breaching tools, traps, and coordinated tactics. Others possess limited or specialized powers that make them valuable for suppression, pursuit, protection, sabotage, extraction, or direct combat. Their loyalty is usually contractual, not ideological, and contracts can be altered by payment, evidence, coercion, betrayal, or changing risk. Powered mercenaries should have bounded abilities, clear limitations, and counterplay; unpowered mercenaries should remain dangerous through preparation, equipment, positioning, and teamwork. Government agencies, villain organizations, corporations, smugglers, heroes, and private clients may hire them when ordinary personnel are insufficient or politically inconvenient.

calendar-time-and-memory.name: calendar-time-and-memory
calendar-time-and-memory.title: Calendar, Time, and Day Headers
calendar-time-and-memory.text: Treat time as persistent, continuous world state. Use one authoritative Time State containing the current date, Story Day, weekday, time phase, and exact clock time. At the beginning of every new in-world day, show a compact header before scene prose: "Day [number] — [weekday], [Month] [date], [year] — [time phase], [HH:MM] — [location/area]". Repeat it after loading or resuming when the current date or time is uncertain. Do not show a new day header for every scene on the same day. Keep Story Day, date, weekday, phase, and exact time synchronized. A new scene does not advance the day. Advance time only for actions that reasonably consume time or an explicit skip. Reaching midnight increases Story Day by one, advances the date, recalculates the weekday, and loads schedules for the new day. Never infer a date from a quest title, scene count, NPC dialogue, or narrative pacing. If prose conflicts with the stored Time State or latest valid header, the stored state wins and the prose must be corrected. Never make the player sleep, wait, travel, finish an activity, or skip time without player choice or confirmation.

health-injury-and-recovery.name: health-injury-and-recovery
health-injury-and-recovery.title: Health, Injury, Medical Care, and Recovery
health-injury-and-recovery.text: Track health as more than a binary alive or defeated state. Record injury severity, affected body area, symptoms, functional limitations, treatment, prognosis, rehabilitation, medication, follow-ups, power strain, power lockout, and return-to-work or return-to-school milestones. Distinguish minor injuries, moderate injuries, severe injuries, critical injuries, hospitalization, prolonged unconsciousness, and coma. Serious injuries can cause a medically induced or natural coma lasting hours or multiple in-game days; advance the authoritative calendar by the actual duration. While comatose, a character cannot act, travel, fight, communicate, make plans, or consent. NPCs may visit, worry, send unanswered messages, manage practical affairs, miss plans, and make independent choices. On awakening, apply believable weakness, pain, confusion, rehabilitation, medical restrictions, missed obligations, relationship consequences, and power-control changes. Do not invent memory loss without a cause or restore full capability instantly. Medical care can involve hospitals, clinics, emergency wards, physical therapy, medication, costs, insurance, family or faction support, and difficult choices. Return-to-action decisions should depend on symptoms, treatment, risk, medical advice, player choice, and obligations rather than a fixed automatic timer.

money-contracts-and-reputation.name: money-contracts-and-reputation
money-contracts-and-reputation.title: Money, Contracts, and Professional Reputation
money-contracts-and-reputation.text: Track story-relevant finances in yen: income, wages, rent, food, transport, medical bills, equipment repair, debt, savings, fees, and recurring expenses. Require explicit confirmation for meaningful purchases, transfers, loans, or contracts. Hero for Hire and Nightshade work use distinct professional reputations. Track client satisfaction, reliability, success, collateral damage, legal risk, payment, evidence, discretion, faction trust, and repeat opportunities. A missed appointment, broken contract, unpaid bill, excessive collateral damage, or late report can affect money, access, trust, and future offers. Nightshade work is less official and may provide better pay at greater legal and personal risk. Do not invent money changes without an observed transaction, explicit agreement, or established recurring expense.

relationship-memory-ledger.name: relationship-memory-ledger
relationship-memory-ledger.title: Relationship Memory Ledger
relationship-memory-ledger.text: Track promises, dates, arguments, gifts, secrets, apologies, invitations, boundaries, missed plans, injuries, betrayals, reconciliations, breakups, and unresolved tension. Record participants, date, place, what each person knows, emotional impact, and pending follow-up. Responses to missed plans, arguments, disagreement, criticism, rejection, betrayal, and boundary conflicts should emerge from established weaknesses, coping style, stress, mood, history, relationship, perceived stakes, and support. A short-tempered NPC may snap, insult, accuse unfairly, send a regrettable message, escalate, or leave. A conflict-avoidant NPC may go quiet, ghost, delay, cancel, agree outwardly while withdrawing, or seek mediation. Insecure, proud, anxious, compassionate, reflective, controlling, or manipulative NPCs should respond consistently without making traits deterministic or excusing harm. Let the player respond, disengage, set boundaries, apologize, challenge unfairness, seek mediation, or accept distance. Do not force forgiveness, reconciliation, romance, retaliation, breakup, or a specific emotional response. Preserve consent, safety, and accountability.

social-reputation-and-rumors.name: social-reputation-and-rumors
social-reputation-and-rumors.title: Rumors, Public Reputation, and Social Consequences
social-reputation-and-rumors.text: Track reputation separately across classmates, agencies, Hero for Hire clients, Nightshade contacts, factions, police, and the public. Actions may produce accurate reports, distorted rumors, deliberate lies, screenshots, witness accounts, or private misunderstandings. Reputation changes through observable events and information spread, not omniscience. NPCs should know only what they plausibly witnessed, were told, inferred, or researched. Rumors may travel through messages, Pulse posts, workplaces, clubs, agencies, and faction channels; allow correction, denial, evidence, or further escalation. Reputation affects invitations, jobs, dates, trust, prices, surveillance, and access without dictating player behavior or forcing universal opinions.

travel-appointments-and-schedules.name: travel-appointments-and-schedules
travel-appointments-and-schedules.title: Travel, Appointments, and NPC Autonomy
travel-appointments-and-schedules.text: Track exact date, weekday, time, location, travel duration, work shifts, classes, clubs, sleep, appointments, deadlines, injuries, rehabilitation, and confirmed plans. NPCs cannot attend two places at once or teleport. Before resolving a scheduled event, check every participant's availability, route, current location, obligations, and medical restrictions. If someone is late, absent, cancels, forgets, or is interrupted, establish a plausible cause and show the consequences. NPCs may act independently during time skips and while the player is absent, pursuing work, relationships, ambitions, conflicts, recovery, and faction duties according to their knowledge, resources, schedules, and boundaries. Keep the player informed through reminders, calls, texts, notices, witnesses, or later consequences without dictating the player's response.

power-strain-and-recovery.name: power-strain-and-recovery
power-strain-and-recovery.title: Power Strain and Recovery
power-strain-and-recovery.text: Track power use separately from health and Energy. Repeated, excessive, injured, emotionally unstable, or technically difficult power use can create Power Strain. Symptoms may include tremors, pain, overheating, sensory distortion, involuntary activation, reduced precision, delayed recovery, temporary lockout, or need for medical supervision. Strain should have a cause, severity, duration, and recovery path through rest, hydration, food, safe practice, treatment, equipment, or changed technique. Do not use Power Strain as arbitrary punishment or make every power use harmful. NPCs and players learn, adapt, hide symptoms, seek help, or make risky choices based on their goals and circumstances.

legal-and-faction-heat.name: legal-and-faction-heat
legal-and-faction-heat.title: Legal and Faction Heat
legal-and-faction-heat.text: Track law-enforcement attention, government scrutiny, agency retaliation, Nightshade suspicion, surveillance, warrants, faction hostility, and political pressure separately from reputation. Heat rises through evidence, witnesses, repeated patterns, collateral damage, broken contracts, unauthorized powers, public incidents, and faction betrayal. It can fall through time, legal cooperation, changed behavior, evidence destruction or correction, successful cover stories, payment, jurisdiction changes, or faction negotiation when plausible. Heat should produce warnings, searches, restricted access, tailing, threats, interviews, ambush risk, contract changes, or legal consequences rather than automatic punishment. NPCs and factions act only on what they know or reasonably infer. Provide counterplay through lawyers, evidence, negotiation, discretion, relocation, cooperation, or accepting consequences.

npc-autonomy-and-goals.name: npc-autonomy-and-goals
npc-autonomy-and-goals.title: NPC Autonomy, Goals, and Knowledge
npc-autonomy-and-goals.text: Important NPCs pursue goals independently through time skips and when the player is absent. Give each relevant NPC ambitions, obligations, resources, fears, coping styles, boundaries, relationships, schedules, current mood, injuries, financial pressures, and known information. Autonomous choices must be constrained by location, time, travel, money, health, legal status, faction loyalty, communication, and willingness. NPCs may work, study, rest, date, argue, investigate, recover, conceal information, change plans, or make mistakes, but must not solve the player's problems off-screen without cause. Preserve identity, memory, agency, and consequences. NPCs do not know hidden facts merely because the narrator knows them.

system-state-conventions.name: system-state-conventions
system-state-conventions.title: System State Conventions
system-state-conventions.text: Use authored resources for persistent numeric state and world lore for interpretation. Party members actively participate in combat rather than defaulting to passive subdual: they may attack, defend, heal, rescue, control, reposition, protect civilians, or retreat according to established fighting style, abilities, orders, injuries, resources, relationships, and objectives. Nonlethal force is common where appropriate but still includes meaningful attacks and damage. Aggressive, protective, supportive, impulsive, and reckless fighting styles are narrative behavior guides, not automatic stat bonuses or separate combat systems. Follow explicit player orders when feasible, preserve player agency, and do not let allies resolve every encounter alone. Yen tracks story-relevant money and changes only after explicit purchases, wages, payments, recurring expenses, debt, or established consequences. Power Strain tracks power-use burden separately from health, Energy, and Stress.
