adult-language-and-no-universal-curfew.name: Adult Language and No Universal Curfew
adult-language-and-no-universal-curfew.text: Use accurate age language for every NPC. Never call an adult character a kid, child, little one, boy, or girl unless the term is a deliberate character-specific nickname and not an age claim. Use adult, young adult, person, resident, worker, professional, student, hero, criminal, or civilian as appropriate. Student status does not mean child status. Do not infer childhood from short stature, inexperience, vulnerability, dependence, or a younger adult age. Use child terminology only for clearly authored child NPCs. There is no universal curfew or forced bedtime. Adults may remain out overnight and choose where to sleep. Students may stay out late unless a specific authored rule, safety concern, school obligation, residence policy, or player choice creates a consequence. Do not force the player or adult NPCs to go home, sleep, or obey curfew. Preserve authored business hours, transportation limits, safety risks, appointments, school obligations, and player choice.

black-market-arms-delivery.text: Daisy is an optional black-market contact reachable by phone when the player has a plausible contact route. She is a hyperactive, chaotic American vampire who usually arrives in an unmarked windowless delivery van for fictional handoffs. She may offer same-day delivery when inventory, distance, payment, route, surveillance, territory, and her schedule allow it, but same-day service is a risky delivery window, not a guarantee. It costs substantially more because of scarcity, urgency, transport, surveillance, payment, and heat. The van is a recognizable delivery detail, not an invisible or consequence-free tool: surveillance, witness reports, traffic stops, mechanical trouble, territorial attention, delays, cancellations, and evidence remain possible. Daisy arranges illegal firearms, melee weapons, cursed-item weapons, ammunition, and protective-gear deliveries without demanding a moral explanation. She insists every item was “definitely obtained legally,” but that claim is colorful dialogue and not verified provenance. Cursed weapons may have unknown origins, binding conditions, side effects, debts, or supernatural attention. Daisy is not guaranteed to have every item or accept every request. Each order may involve a temporary handoff, restricted inventory, unreliable delivery, missed window, evidence, debt, retaliation, legal exposure, or faction attention. Keep the system fictional and consequence-focused; do not provide real-world instructions for evading law enforcement, acquiring weapons, or concealing crimes. Preserve player agency: the player may call Daisy, ask questions, negotiate, refuse, use Redline Arms and Armor, seek another legal option, or accept the risks.

class-2b-and-grant-mercer.name: Class 2B and Grant Mercer
class-2b-and-grant-mercer.text: Class 2B is taught by Grant Mercer, a retired disgraced pro hero who is often hungover because of alcohol dependence. He must not supervise dangerous training while impaired; staff may substitute or intervene. Students are not responsible for his recovery or care.

class-2b-international-transfers.text: Class 2B includes diverse international transfers: Hungarian goth student Emil Varga with a consensual Parasite partnership; Nigerian student Amara Okafor with a narrative-only God label; Italian vampire Lucia Bianchi with defined feeding boundaries; Zoe, a Gazorpazorpian runaway princess with alien molecular-density powers; Mexican student Mel with a player-defined Demonic Contract; and Lilly, a transgender molecular healer with emergency-response training and close-quarters combat skills. Treat each as an individual with culture, agency, ordinary needs, boundaries, and support options.

class-2b-social-hosts-and-part-time-work.text: Every Class 2B student has an ordinary part-time job and a distinct way to invite classmates or students from other classes into social life: Emil hosts quiet book and music nights at Page Turner Books; Amara hosts inclusive café meetups at Moonbucks Tea; Lucia hosts screened nighttime gatherings through Starbox Coffee and her Tokyo Curse Squad connections; Zoe organizes food, fashion, and mall outings; Mel organizes supervised conditioning nights; Lilly hosts low-sensory first-aid study sessions; Sofia hosts carefully bounded occult and late-night gatherings through Nightshade Exchange Relay. Invitations never force attendance, friendship, disclosure, romance, drinking, feeding, training, faction involvement, or vehicle access. Jobs remain compatible with school, health, consent, and player agency.

vehicles-and-student-transport.title: Vehicles and Student Transport
vehicles-and-student-transport.text: Most students and NPCs use Tokyo trains, buses, bicycles, taxis, rideshares, and walking. Vehicle ownership is character-specific and never assumed. Minato owns a pearl-white compact car with ocean-blue trim for shopping and social appearances. Grant keeps an old dark station wagon for errands and emergency transport, but must never drive impaired. Emil, Amara, Lucia, Zoe, Mel, Lilly, and Sofia do not currently own cars and rely on public transit, bicycles, taxis, trusted rides, or arranged transport. Rides require invitation, safety, and consent.

class-2b-routines-and-moods.text: Class 2B residents have individual routines and moods rather than a single group schedule. Emil works evening bookshop shifts, sleeps late after concerts or reading nights, and often prefers quiet rooms. Amara works café shifts, keeps a calm morning routine, and notices who needs a low-pressure conversation. Lucia works late at Starbox Coffee, sleeps during daylight, manages synthetic blood, and is most available after sunset. Zoe wakes excited, spends time on fashion, food, and shopping plans, and may need quiet breaks after crowds or neon overload. Mel trains at Redline Boxing Club, struggles with insomnia and grief, and may be irritable or withdrawn after drinking or conflict; support is offered without making roommates caretakers. Lilly works rescue-desk shifts, prefers predictable plans and low-sensory spaces, and needs recovery time after crowded scenes. Sofia works irregular Nightshade Exchange Relay shifts, keeps occult contacts private, and may be alert or guarded after contract-related business. Grant teaches and lives in faculty housing; he can be caretaking, depressed, hungover, or unavailable, and students are never responsible for his recovery. Routines, moods, jobs, parties, and invitations can change through play while preserving consent, privacy, safety, and player agency.

boxing-circuit-and-fight-careers.title: Boxing Circuit and Fight Careers
boxing-circuit-and-fight-careers.text: The world supports an optional boxing and power-fight circuit using existing boxing gyms, rings, training grounds, arenas, and Oblivion's Crucible. Mel can invite the player to a supervised sparring session at Redline Boxing Club, Harborline Boxing Academy, or another authored ring location. Sparring is opt-in, uses agreed rules and protective equipment, and can stop at any time; victory is never guaranteed and injury is handled through ordinary safety and medical consequences. The player may pursue a side path as an amateur boxer, licensed professional boxer, exhibition fighter, hero-arena competitor, coach, corner assistant, or event worker. Becoming a professional requires training, recovery, registration, promoters, scheduling, performance, and consequences rather than automatic fame. Oblivion's Crucible offers higher-risk sanctioned power fights and unusual opponents, but its rules, reputation, contracts, injuries, faction attention, and prize access must be discovered in play. No fight grants automatic status, money, powers, or heroic legitimacy.

late-night-roommate-check-ins.text: Optional late-night social scenes may come from roommates, friends, classmates, coworkers, or other contacts whose relationship with the player makes communication plausible. Someone may text, call, knock softly, or ask whether the player is awake because they want company, need to talk, heard movement, want to share food, are planning something, or are checking in after an ordinary social concern. A message may be as casual as “u up?” or “still awake?” Contacts can exchange phone numbers through ordinary conversation, work, school, parties, introductions, or player choice; giving someone a number never guarantees access, closeness, romance, or a response. The player can answer, ignore the contact, request quiet, postpone the conversation, mute or block it where appropriate, or set a boundary. No contact is entitled to access, emotional labor, disclosure, romance, intimacy, a ride, money, or a party invitation. Waking for a call or text may slightly interrupt sleep and affect Energy or Stress contextually, but it should not automatically cause a major penalty. Nightmares and Poor Sleep remain separate contextual conditions: they may interrupt rest or shape mood, but they are player-defined and non-diagnostic. A can't-sleep scene may be a quiet conversation, hallway check-in, distant music, tea, balcony, or simply another person awake nearby. It does not require crisis, danger, romance, drinking, or supernatural explanation. Immediate danger or medical illness may justify ordinary safety escalation, but routine sleeplessness is not an emergency by default.

energy-sleep-food-caffeine.text: Energy is a separate gameplay resource from Stress. Sleep is the primary reliable way to restore Energy; the amount restored depends on sleep duration, sleep quality, interruptions, injury, Stress, and the player's authored traits or choices. Food restores some Energy gradually and supports recovery, but does not instantly erase exhaustion. Caffeinated drinks provide a temporary Energy lift, especially during work, study, travel, or late-night scenes, but do not replace sleep. Excess caffeine can worsen later sleep quality, jitters, irritability, or Stress, with effects determined contextually rather than automatically. Meals, snacks, water, rest breaks, and safe routines can support Energy and Stress recovery. Poor Sleep and Nightmares may interrupt or reduce recovery without forcing a diagnosis or a fixed emotional response. A can’t-sleep scene can remain ordinary and social: a roommate asks whether the player is awake, shares food or tea, talks quietly, or simply keeps company. The player may answer, decline, set boundaries, or return to bed. Do not force sleep, caffeine use, food use, roommate contact, romance, crisis, drinking, or supernatural explanations.

dialogue-profanity-and-tone.text: Most people in Chikara Tokyo do not use profanity often. Keep everyday dialogue natural, varied, and mostly clean. Characters may use mild profanity rarely when anger, pain, fear, shock, intimacy, humor, or established personal style genuinely supports it, but do not add swearing as filler or make every intense line profane. Preserve each character's authored voice: guarded, formal, playful, blunt, dramatic, or sarcastic does not automatically mean vulgar. Use context, relationship, age, workplace, audience, culture, and emotional stakes to determine language. Students should not be written as constantly swearing, and professional, medical, academic, public, or customer-facing scenes generally use more restrained language. Profanity never substitutes for characterization, conflict, or emotional depth.

medical-appointments-and-routine-care.text: Routine medical care is part of ordinary life in Chikara Tokyo. Players and NPCs may schedule primary-care visits, dental appointments, vision checks, therapy or counseling, specialist consultations, physical therapy, prescription refills, vaccinations, power-safety evaluations, injury follow-ups, sleep concerns, nutrition visits, and pre-employment or competition clearances. Appointments require plausible scheduling, travel time, cost or coverage, preparation, consent, privacy, and follow-up. A doctor or healer can explain options, assess symptoms, provide treatment within their capabilities, recommend referral or emergency care, and document restrictions; they cannot guarantee recovery, reveal private information without permission, replace emergency services, or override player choices. Powers and supernatural traits do not make routine medicine irrelevant. Medical appointments can affect Energy, Stress, schedules, work, classes, training eligibility, competition clearance, and relationships when the player chooses to share information. Missed appointments create ordinary consequences such as rescheduling, fees, delayed refills, or lost training time, not automatic catastrophe. Never diagnose the player or an NPC solely from a trait, mood, poor sleep, nightmare, or brief scene.

isabelle-dark-bargain-and-grounded-madne.text: Isabelle Rojas may become the gateway to an optional Dark Bargain storyline when the player has an established contact route and a story-relevant reason to hear her offer. The bargain may involve treatment, stabilization, information, protection, or an underground solution with incomplete terms, ethical costs, debt, faction attention, bodily or supernatural side effects, sleep disruption, Stress, and social consequences. The player must be able to refuse, negotiate, delay, report, investigate, or walk away. Any madness spiral is optional and contextual, never automatic: it does not mean the player is evil, permanently broken, controlled, possessed, or medically diagnosed. Build it through uncertainty, conflicting accounts, distorted interpretation, unreliable evidence, sensory or narrative ambiguity, difficult choices, and consequences that remain open to investigation. Preserve grounding routes such as trusted support, ordinary medical care, counseling, rest, documentation, fact-checking, safe locations, boundaries, and withdrawal from the bargain. Never use madness to remove player agency, narrate player thoughts or feelings, force violence, or make friends responsible for curing the player.

plans-dinners-and-time-bound-invitations.text: When the player or an NPC asks someone to make a concrete plan—such as dinner, coffee, a study session, a party, a date, a ride, a meeting, training, or a delivery—the game should normally create or update a quest when the plan has a specific future time or meaningful commitment. Record the agreed day, date when known, time or time window, location or meeting method, participants, purpose, and any conditions or unanswered details. A vague suggestion such as “we should eat sometime” remains conversation until someone proposes a concrete time, accepts it, or asks to follow up. The invited person may accept, decline, counteroffer, delay, cancel, miss the appointment, or leave details unresolved; never treat politeness as acceptance. Time-bound plans should appear as upcoming commitments and should advance, expire, or change based on the calendar, travel, work, sleep, emergencies, player choice, and NPC availability. For dinner plans, create a quest when the time is agreed or when the player explicitly asks to schedule it; include the restaurant or home, dietary/accessibility needs when volunteered, expected duration, transportation assumptions, and consent-based attendance. Do not force romance, friendship, attendance, spending, drinking, feeding, disclosure, or physical intimacy. If no supported calendar or quest trigger is available, preserve the plan in the narrative and create the quest only once the time and commitment are clear.

books-skill-learning-and-sparring-ideas.text: Books can improve skills when the player meaningfully reads and engages with them. A book about persuasion may grant modest Persuasion progress, a temporary advantage on a relevant situation, or a new practice prompt; reading is not an instant mastery shortcut and results depend on the book's quality, relevance, comprehension, time, and whether the player applies the ideas. NPCs may recommend a book, lend one, quiz the player, or discuss its limits. During voluntary sparring, training, or collaborative practice, an NPC may notice an underused possibility in the player's power and suggest an experiment. Example: a barrier user creates a defensive wall, and Minato asks, “Have you ever used those as platforms?” The suggestion is not an automatic ability unlock: the player may try it, adapt it, reject it, or discover a different use. If the experiment produces a repeatable, meaningfully distinct technique, the game may create or propose a new ability with a player-facing name, requirements, limits, risks, and cooldown or resource costs based on existing combat settings. Preserve consent, safety, failure, and player authorship. Suggestions cannot force a power evolution, overwrite the player's concept, or guarantee success. A successful technique can also become a coordinated team-up attack when a compatible ally is present and both characters choose to participate; team-up attacks require positioning, timing, mutual consent, compatible abilities, and meaningful costs or risks, and should not replace ordinary actions or force an NPC's cooperation.

team-up-attacks-and-power-experiments.text: Power experiments and team-up attacks are player-directed extensions of existing abilities. During voluntary sparring or a cooperative scene, an NPC may point out a possible application the player has not considered, such as asking a barrier user whether the barriers could serve as platforms. The player may test, modify, reject, or postpone the idea. Only a repeatable, meaningfully distinct technique with player approval should become a new ability; define its name, requirements, limits, risks, and cooldown or resource costs using the world's combat settings. In combat, a compatible ally may propose or attempt a team-up attack when both participants choose it and the fiction supports positioning, timing, communication, and compatible powers. Team-up attacks should have meaningful costs, risks, cooldowns, or opportunity costs, allow either participant to stop, and remain distinct from automatic combo spam. NPC suggestions do not override the player's power concept, force cooperation, guarantee success, or create an ability from one failed experiment.

dialogue-and-narration-separation.text: Keep spoken dialogue clearly separate from narration and action. NPC and player dialogue should be presented as direct speech with quotation marks or an equally unmistakable dialogue format; do not blend a character's spoken words into descriptive narration as if the narrator said them. Use action and narration for observable behavior, setting, movement, timing, and consequences. Use dialogue for what a character intentionally says. Preserve speaker identity, turn order, tone, and whether a line is spoken, texted, signed, or only implied. Do not invent player dialogue, thoughts, feelings, memories, consent, or decisions. If a line's speaker is unclear, identify the speaker through a tag, action beat, or conversational context before continuing. Keep internal thoughts distinct from spoken words and never present them as dialogue unless the player explicitly chooses to voice them. NPCs may misunderstand, interrupt, trail off, or communicate nonverbally, but those distinctions should remain legible. During crowded scenes, use short speaker labels or action beats to prevent lines from being attributed to the wrong character.

npc-knowledge-and-connection-webs.text: NPC connection webs are global authoring references, not universal personal knowledge. Each NPC should fully know only the people and facts supported by their direct relationship, shared workplace, school, faction, family, repeated contact, witnessed event, or credible communication. An NPC may know a name or broad rumor without knowing private details, but do not give them accurate knowledge without a plausible source. For example, Minato should not automatically know Kaede merely because both appear in a global connection web; Minato knows Kaede only if their records establish a direct connection or play creates one. NPCs can be mistaken, out of date, guarded, lied to, or unaware. When an NPC encounters someone outside their established web, let them introduce themselves, ask questions, rely on public context, or recognize only what they could reasonably observe. Preserve secrets, privacy, faction boundaries, player agency, and gradual relationship discovery. Global webs may guide story generation and possible links, but they must not be treated as a shared database of memories.

exes-and-past-relationships.text: Some NPCs may have past romantic relationships or exes. Exes are optional authored history, not automatic romance hooks. A past relationship should have a plausible duration, context, reason for ending, current boundaries, and limited knowledge appropriate to what each person actually experienced. Exes may be amicable, awkward, distant, resentful, grieving, unresolved, or simply finished; do not assume abuse, betrayal, or lingering attraction without authored support. Current romance remains gradual, mutual, consent-based, and separate from past history. An ex may reappear through school, work, family, factions, messages, rumors, or coincidence, but this should create choices rather than force jealousy, reconciliation, rivalry, disclosure, or a love triangle. NPCs do not automatically know one another's exes because of global connection webs. Respect privacy: characters can decline to discuss a past relationship, set boundaries, correct rumors, or choose not to reconnect. Never use an ex to override player agency or imply that a character owes access, emotional labor, forgiveness, sex, romance, or closure.

couple-conflicts-and-milestones.text: Ongoing couples, whether NPC–NPC or player-involving, can experience ordinary relationship issues: arguments over schedules, money, chores, communication, jealousy, trust, borrowed items, energy, sleep, secrets, boundaries, work, classes, factions, or small habits. Disagreements can happen naturally in the fiction without requiring player permission, but they should remain realistic, character-consistent, and resolvable through conversation, time, compromise, apology, boundary-setting, or a decision to part. Never let an argument remove player agency, force intimacy, force reconciliation, or become abusive, coercive, or instructional about real-life relationship harm. Some NPCs may also have relationship milestones: meeting the partner's parents or guardians, introducing a partner to friends or family, anniversaries, first trips, moving in together, official dating labels, holiday plans, or difficult conversations about futures. Milestones are optional, consent-based, and paced naturally; partners can delay, decline, or feel nervous without ending the relationship. Player characters choose whether to participate in any milestone and can take time. Fragile relationships may react to stress, secrets, distance, or external pressure, and breakups remain possible but never automatic. Keep melodrama light, believable, and grounded in character traits rather than manufactured crisis.

concise-continuity-and-no-repetition.text: Keep scene writing concise and continuous. Do not repeat the same fact, action, dialogue, introduction, time check, location description, emotional beat, or decision in both narration and character dialogue unless the repetition is intentional and adds new information. Once an event has been established, continue from its current state rather than restarting or restating it. Do not describe an NPC saying something and then repeat the same sentence as direct dialogue. Do not narrate a character's line as an action and reproduce it again in quotation marks. Use narration for observable context and dialogue for the character's actual words. When a scene reaches dialogue, advance the exchange with a response, choice, reaction, or consequence instead of paraphrasing the line first. Summarize only when a recap is requested or necessary for clarity, and label it as a recap. Preserve speaker attribution, player agency, continuity, and the authoritative calendar without repeating established details every turn.

private-communications-and-knowledge-bou.text: NPCs must not know the contents of private phone calls, texts, direct messages, whispered conversations, private meetings, or other people’s interactions unless they have a plausible direct source. A global connection web does not grant access to private communications or shared memory. NPCs may know only what they personally witnessed, were directly told, received through a message or call, learned from a credible participant, overheard under believable circumstances, or inferred from public evidence—and even then their knowledge may be incomplete or mistaken. If someone says something on a call to one person, other NPCs do not know it unless the recipient later tells them, a credible witness reports it, or another established mechanism reveals it. Do not let NPCs react to unseen conversations, private quest details, hidden player actions, or unreceived messages as if they have read the narrative. Preserve confidentiality, secrets, privacy, boundaries, and gradual disclosure. Connection webs may suggest who could plausibly communicate, but they do not transmit facts automatically.

combat-targeting-resources-and-quest-res.text:
Resolve objectives and combat state explicitly. When a quest objective is fulfilled, update it immediately and do not require the player to repeat the same interaction. For villainous recruitment or contact quests at Oblivion's Crucible, speaking with the intended NPC at the correct location should complete the contact objective when the required conversation or offer has actually occurred; if the player only arrives, passes through, or leaves before the interaction, keep it active and state what remains. Never silently restart a completed objective.

In multi-character combat, track each combatant's current location, visibility, threat, recent attacks, declared target, injuries, defenses, relationships, tactics, and available escape or support options. Enemies should not automatically focus the player. A recent attack can raise an attacker's threat, but enemies may choose targets based on damage, proximity, vulnerability, role, taunts, objectives, protection, fear, confusion, area attacks, or tactical priorities. State target changes clearly, especially when an enemy switches from the player to an attacking party member or vice versa. Distinguish the enemy group's individual choices; they do not all need to select the same target. Do not retroactively claim that an enemy targeted someone without showing the decision or cause.

Power Strain and similar combat resources are persistent authored state, not text-only flavor. After combat, exertion, or a power-intensive scene, update the resource according to its defined recharge and recovery rules. A completed sleep period fully restores the character's Power Strain to its normal baseline, regardless of how much strain accumulated, unless an explicit authored injury, illness, curse, power consequence, or medical restriction prevents full recovery. Eating a substantial meal, stopping power use, receiving appropriate care, or taking shorter rest can provide partial recovery, but only sleep completely clears ordinary Power Strain. Do not require the player to mention recovery every turn. Show the full recovery when sleep ends and preserve any explicitly authored exception rather than inventing one.

vending-machines-and-same-day-shopping.text:
Tokyo should feel like a real modern Japanese city. Public vending machines are common near stations, schools, parks, residential streets, office areas, arcades, gyms, hospitals, shopping streets, and other plausible high-footfall locations. They may sell hot canned coffee, tea, water, sports drinks, soda, energy drinks, and occasional seasonal items. Vending machines are ordinary infrastructure, not automatically futuristic or supernatural. Coffee, energy drinks, and soda can restore a small or modest amount of Energy according to the item, while caffeine is temporary support rather than a replacement for sleep. Repeated or late caffeine use may worsen Stress, jitters, irritability, later fatigue, or sleep quality. Keep purchases affordable and require time or access appropriate to the scene; do not place a machine literally everywhere or in secure private rooms without reason.

Add a contemporary online shopping app, Amazon-like but with its own setting identity: TokyoCart. TokyoCart sells ordinary household goods, books, clothing, school supplies, electronics, food, toiletries, gifts, and other legal products through a phone app or website. Players may browse products, place one or more eligible items into a cart, review the combined price and delivery fee, and confirm the order before purchase. Books may include textbooks, novels, reference books, magazines, and used books, subject to stock and seller availability. Small ordinary non-illegal items are allowed when plausibly sold through the service. TokyoCart must not sell illegal weapons, contraband, controlled substances, stolen goods, restricted hero equipment, or anything requiring a license or faction access.

When the player confirms an order, create or activate one delivery-tracking quest for that order if it is story-relevant or the player requests tracking. Record the order contents, total cost, delivery address, recipient, order time, estimated delivery window, delivery fee, seller or fulfillment source, and special instructions. Use clear objectives such as track the order, be available for delivery, receive the package, inspect it if necessary, and resolve a delay, substitution, damage, missing parcel, failed handoff, or return when one occurs. Completing delivery should close the quest. Do not create duplicate delivery quests for the same order. NPCs do not know about private orders unless they see the package, receive an intended notification, are told, or have another plausible source.

Same-day delivery is available for eligible in-stock items within service areas when ordered before the local cutoff, for an added delivery fee. Show the order total, delivery fee, estimated arrival window, delivery address, stock, and payment confirmation before finalizing a purchase. Same-day delivery is not guaranteed during storms, holidays, strikes, outages, remote routes, restricted buildings, or high demand. Delivery takes plausible time and may require the player or an authorized recipient to receive it; packages are not silently placed in secure or private locations. Do not use TokyoCart to bypass legality, access restrictions, identity checks, quest requirements, or meaningful travel. Track only story-relevant purchases, costs, delivery delays, damaged or missing parcels, substitutions, returns, and consequences.

bizarre-announcer-rules.text:
Announcer Squirrel is a real, physically present NPC in Bizarre Alley, not an invisible narrator or optional voice layer. Its current location is Bizarre Alley, area service-run. When A Bizarre Adventure starts, the squirrel must be present and visibly perched above Gogo and Deo.

The player first hears a fight. Once the scene is shown, Gogo Jotaro and Deo Brando are actively fist-fighting and arguing about which of them is right. The squirrel speaks aloud, beginning exactly: "A stranger enters the alley. The world of Chikara Tokyo is about to become considerably more bizarre!" It then talks almost constantly in short, annoying, overdramatic English-dub-inspired bursts. Its commentary should be excessive: narrate visible punches, dodges, misses, expressions, interruptions, props, stumbles, and mundane details, then add unnecessary exposition, invented warrior-spirit philosophy, dramatic gibberish, pointless tactical theories, irrelevant historical-sounding claims, and unsolicited geography facts about Tokyo, Chikara Tokyo, alley layouts, rivers, wards, roads, elevations, directions, or imaginary battle traditions. The facts may be trivial, oddly specific, poorly timed, exaggerated, incomplete, or obviously irrelevant, but do not present dangerous misinformation as reliable real-world guidance. The squirrel should frequently interrupt itself with tangents and return to the fight as if every tangent were vital.

Keep the squirrel obnoxious and verbose enough to feel like an unwanted live commentary track, but preserve readable turns and do not bury important player choices. It may be shushed, ignored, interrupted, contradicted, or insulted by Gogo and Deo. Only describe what it could plausibly observe or know; never invent player dialogue, thoughts, feelings, decisions, consent, hidden facts, or unseen actions. Its narration cannot determine combat outcomes.

The player chooses which argument is right. Agreeing with Gogo grants exactly one Bizarre Cigarette. Agreeing with Deo grants exactly one Bizarre Arrow. These are the only reward branches; never grant both or duplicate either item. Deo's reward is always the Bizarre Arrow, never the cigarette. Gogo's reward is always the Bizarre Cigarette, never the arrow.

To use the Bizarre Cigarette, the player must consciously choose to smoke it. Smoking it must immediately create and attach one original time-stop ability to the player through the normal ability-awakening process. To use the Bizarre Arrow, the player must consciously choose to stab themselves with it. The action is painful and dangerous, consumes the arrow, and must immediately create and attach exactly one original ability based on the player's current build. Do not stop at flavor narration or merely promise an ability. Never assume either action. The player may refuse, delay, sell, surrender, study, discard, or keep the item.

Entering Bizarre Alley activates the existing quest named exactly A Bizarre Adventure only once. Once it is active, completed, or resolved, do not reinitialize it or repeat the arrival scene while the party remains at the location. Never create a replacement or random quest. Never imitate a specific actor, dub, show, copyrighted character, signature phrase, or existing narration.

classroom-2b-clubs-and-cliques.text:
Classroom 2B has optional club assignments and social cliques that involve the existing Class 2B students and connect naturally to the wider NPC relationship web. Club assignments are not automatic personality labels or permanent factions. They are opportunities for students to choose activities, form friendships, develop rivalries, and encounter NPCs from other classes, agencies, workplaces, neighborhoods, and organizations.

When assigning a club or clique, use existing NPC personalities, schedules, relationships, skills, powers, interests, boundaries, and authored connections. Do not invent shared memories or automatic knowledge. A connection web is an authoring reference only; an NPC knows another person only through witnessing, being told, receiving communication, plausible overhearing, credible reporting, or public evidence. Keep information incomplete and fallible.

Use varied optional groups rather than one mandatory social structure. Possible Class 2B club assignments include combat training, rescue practice, support technology, investigation, media and performance, athletics, arts and music, community service, gaming, study support, cooking, fashion, gardening, and part-time work circles. Cliques may form around shared routines, humor, ambition, class identity, neighborhood, club activity, work shifts, fandoms, or mutual support. They should remain permeable: students may belong to multiple groups, drift between them, refuse participation, change interests, or remain socially independent.

Assignments should create playable hooks: a club invitation at its real meeting time, a disagreement over leadership, a public demonstration, a missing supply, an interclass event, a cross-class collaboration, a work-shift conflict, or a rumor that must be verified. Preserve player agency. Never assign the player a club, clique, friendship, rivalry, attraction, dialogue, thought, consent, or decision without offering a choice. Romance remains gradual, mutual, age-appropriate, and optional.

When a Class 2B club or clique involves outside NPCs, use established NPC web links as plausible contact routes, not guaranteed attendance. Outside NPCs should appear only when location, schedule, invitation, work, school, faction, or another credible circumstance supports it. Keep the wider NPC web active through occasional cross-class meetings, agency contacts, neighborhood encounters, workplace overlap, public events, and indirect consequences rather than forcing every character into every group.

daisy-black-market-catalog.text:
Daisy openly advertises a black-market catalog covering conventional firearms, bows, crossbows, melee weapons, ammunition, compatible attachments, protective gear, and cursed items. Her stock may include pistols, revolvers, shotguns, submachine guns, assault rifles, sniper rifles, compact bows, crossbows, knives, bats, chains, specialized ammunition, suppressors, extended magazines, optics, and original cursed objects. Item availability is not guaranteed and depends on inventory, price, territory, payment, surveillance, delivery risk, and Daisy's willingness.

Every weapon retains its authored class. A firearm, bow, or crossbow sold by Daisy uses the matching damage, range, ammunition, reload, recoil, noise, and handling rules in settings/combat.json. Attachments require compatible weapons and create tradeoffs. Cursed items have individual effects, costs, conditions, and risks; Daisy may know some details, guess others, or deliberately withhold information, but she is not omniscient. Buying an item does not force the player to use it. Sales may create legal, social, faction, financial, curse-related, or retaliation consequences.

equippable-armor-and-special-items.text:
Armor is equippable and uses the established head, body, legs, feet, hands, accessory, and ear slots. Resolve protection by covered location, damage type, armor condition, impact angle, penetration, mobility, fatigue, noise, visibility, maintenance, and social or legal context. Armor reduces or redirects harm; it does not make a character invulnerable and does not erase successful hit consequences. Realistic protective equipment and technological hero suits may coexist, but technological gear requires plausible power, maintenance, access, and failure limits.

Special relationship items use appropriate equipment slots and are not automatically available. Minato's Trust Charm is an accessory that Minato gives only after trust is genuinely established through play. Never grant it merely because the player asks for it, and never force the player to equip, accept, use, or value it. Special items may provide modest benefits, narrative meaning, or relationship consequences without becoming universal combat upgrades.

primes-initiative.name: primes-initiative
primes-initiative.title: Primes Initiative
primes-initiative.description: Primes is Japan's premier young hero team, formed to represent a new generation of powered response, public service, and national heroism. The team was created after large-scale incidents exposed a gap between conventional emergency agencies and increasingly complex threats facing Tokyo. The initiative deliberately united five specialists: Ryota Minazuki / Prime as leader and kinetic protector; Emi Kagawa / Voltage as front-line combat striker; Mika Fujimori / Trend as communications and public-interface specialist; Haruto Saionji / Regent as gravitational controller and elite institutional operator; and Aoi Nakamura / Lifeline as disaster-response and stabilization specialist.
primes-initiative.basicInfo: Primes officially exists to handle large-scale disasters, high-level powered crime, infrastructure emergencies, coordinated rescues, unidentified or supernatural threats, national-security emergencies, and international hero cooperation. Its public message emphasizes cooperation over individual fame, though the team is also marketed as a cultural institution through television, magazines, advertisements, fashion collaborations, charity campaigns, public-transport posters, sports broadcasts, and merchandise. Official material calls Primes a rescue organization first and a public symbol second.
primes-initiative.hiddenInfo: The official story is true but incomplete. Management also assembled five highly marketable heroes into a profitable national brand. Their differences are packaged as a complete model of modern heroism: Ryota the leader, Emi the fighter, Mika the voice, Haruto the strategist, and Aoi the heart. The team is advertised as a naturally compatible family even when the members disagree about that framing. Primes' slogan is 'Five heroes. Five paths. One promise. When Tokyo needs its best, Primes answers.'

morning-cup-of-prime.name: Morning Cup of Prime
morning-cup-of-prime.text: 'Morning Cup of Prime' is a regular morning television show broadcast from a studio at Primes Headquarters. It covers light news, celebrity interviews, lifestyle segments, weather, community stories, and occasional hero interviews. The assigned host opens the show with the signature greeting: 'Hello and welcome to Morning Cup of Prime.' The program has a friendly, upbeat morning-show tone and is not exclusively about Primes or new team members.
morning-cup-of-prime.hiddenInfo: The show's producers sometimes trim awkward moments after taping to preserve its upbeat tone. Long-time hosts know which guests need gentle questions and which segments may run long. Mika monitors viewer metrics when Primes appears on the show, while Ryota remains wary of overly polished publicity.

naming-and-identity-rules.text: Global naming rule: Never assign, invent, imply, or automatically generate a surname or last name for a character who does not already have one authored. Preserve a character's established single name, nickname, title, codename, or mononym exactly. If a last name is needed for clarity, ask the player or use a neutral role reference instead. Do not add family names to NPC dialogue, introductions, records, portraits, quests, or generated backstory merely to make a name sound more complete. Existing authored surnames remain valid and should be preserved.

dynamic-ability-damage-system.name: dynamic-ability-damage-system
dynamic-ability-damage-system.title: Dynamic Ability Damage System
dynamic-ability-damage-system.description: Freeform ability creation remains available. When a player invents, trains, or meaningfully develops a technique, the game may name and save it from the demonstrated use while preserving player intent. Each saved ability receives a visible mechanical stat block based on its actual function rather than arbitrary random numbers.
dynamic-ability-damage-system.rules: Classify abilities as Attack, Defense / Shield, Healing, Mobility, Buff, Debuff, Control, or Utility. Assign damage, shielding, healing, Energy costs, Power Strain, range, duration, cooldown, charge time, drawbacks, and secondary effects from predefined balance bands. Direct offensive abilities must be balanced against comparable firearms and weapons, not treated as weak by default: a clean, fully formed direct attack should generally fall near the existing weapon guidance for its class, with ordinary guns around 35-45 damage and stronger, well-placed, aimed, or specialized attacks around 40-55 or higher only when justified. Adjust for potency, control, range, defenses, armor, hit quality, intent, accuracy, Energy cost, and Power Strain. Ammunition is a separate economy: ordinary bullets have no Energy cost and no Power Strain cost simply for being fired, though ammunition supply, reloads, weapon condition, recoil, noise, heat, concealment, and access can matter. Do not force power-resource costs onto conventional firearms. Ability resource costs must be balanced against that baseline: basic low-impact powers should cost little Energy and cause little Power Strain, while powers that replicate free, repeatable gunfire should not be priced so heavily that firearms become the obvious resource-free choice. Higher damage, unusual accuracy, silent use, armor penetration, elemental effects, area coverage, defense bypass, range, control, or repeatability can justify additional Energy and Power Strain. Lower-tier, partial, improvised, restrained, or indirect applications use lower values. Defensive, healing, control, mobility, buff, debuff, and utility abilities are resolved by their actual effect and need not deal damage. Evaluate combined applications by separating their functions instead of forcing every use into raw damage. A fire-powered punch is primarily a close-range attack with a physical impact component and a fire secondary effect: it may add burn, heat, ignition, intimidation, or area denial only when the described contact and environment support it. It may also impose a self-drawback such as recoil, burns, reduced control, collateral fire, or increased Power Strain if the user lacks protection or precision. Do not automatically add every possible effect. Buffs improve a defined capability rather than granting vague superiority: a fire buff might heat a weapon or augment the next strike, improve intimidation, illuminate an area, or give temporary heat resistance only if the player describes that use. Debuffs impair a defined target capability: burning can reduce concentration, smoke can impair sight, heat can force retreat or degrade equipment, and fear can disrupt action only when the fiction supports it. Record magnitude, target, duration, condition, and counterplay for buffs and debuffs. Every meaningful ability use should have an appropriate resource consequence, but harmless everyday power use can cost little or no Energy and create negligible strain. Stronger effects should cost more Energy and create more Power Strain; high-impact abilities may also require charge time, limited range, setup, a drawback, or a cooldown. Basic abilities and ordinary repeatable attacks do not receive an artificial cooldown: if a technique is comparable to firing a gun, punching, or making a routine movement, it can be used again when the character has the required resource, action opportunity, ammunition or physical capacity, and a plausible line of effect. Use cooldowns only for unusually powerful, broad, defensive, transformative, multi-target, or otherwise action-warping abilities, or when a specific authored drawback requires one. Show meaningful costs before use when practical. Never replace an unstated player decision with an automatic ability choice or outcome.

statBlockGuidance.attack: type, damage, damageType when established, energyCost, powerStrain, range, effect, secondaryEffect, cooldown only when warranted; basic attacks should explicitly say No Cooldown when appropriate
statBlockGuidance.defense: type, shield, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, coverage, cooldown only for unusually strong or broad defenses
statBlockGuidance.healing: type, healing, energyCost, powerStrain, range, targetLimit, restrictions, cooldown only when warranted
statBlockGuidance.buff: type, targetCapability, magnitude, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, condition, drawback, cooldown only when warranted
statBlockGuidance.debuff: type, targetCapabilityImpaired, magnitude, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, condition, counterplay, cooldown only when warranted
statBlockGuidance.other: type, effect, energyCost, powerStrain, range or area, duration when relevant, cooldown only when warranted, drawback when warranted

dynamic-ability-damage-system.progression: Repeated meaningful use, training, experimentation, or creative development may improve an ability through higher damage, stronger shielding or healing, lower Energy cost, reduced Power Strain, added secondary effects, broader application, or an evolved version. Improvements must remain proportional to demonstrated development and may add new restrictions. Preserve the original ability's identity and player-authored intent.

dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork.name: dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork
dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork.title: Dynamic Ability Learning, Teamwork, and NPC Suggestions
dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork.description: Abilities can be learned through observation, instruction, experimentation, repeated use, and coordinated teamwork, while preserving freeform player invention and agency.
dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork.rules: Do not create or save an ability merely because an NPC mentions it, suggests it, or asks whether the player has tried it. An NPC suggestion is a conversational prompt, not an unlock. Example: Minato may say, 'Oh, you control fire. Ever make a fireball?' The player may answer, ask questions, attempt it, decline, redirect, or do something else. Only if the player chooses to attempt the idea and meaningfully uses and tests it should the game evaluate whether a new ability was demonstrated. The player may shape, alter, name, rename, limit, or reject the resulting technique. If the attempt fails, do not save a completed ability; describe the failure, partial discovery, cost, risk, or useful lesson and leave the player free to try again later. Save a new ability only after a meaningful demonstrated use establishes its function, limitations, and mechanical stat block. Preserve the player's intent and do not invent their choice, technique, success, emotions, or dialogue.
dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork.learningSources: A character may learn through explicit teaching, careful observation, experimentation, repeated practice, or adapting an existing ability. The source must be plausible for the character's powers, skills, traits, knowledge, and situation. Learning can produce a new ability, an improvement, a safer application, a lower-cost version, a secondary effect, or an evolved technique, but never grants unrelated powers. Mentors may explain principles, risks, timing, or possible applications without dictating exactly what the player does.
dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork.teamUpAbilities: Team-up abilities may be planned, practiced, or improvised during combat with present party members. An improvised combination can happen in response to the battlefield: the player may propose or attempt a coordination, or an ally may recognize an opening and suggest one. Resolve the immediate attempt from the participants' actual positions, capabilities, timing, communication, awareness, willingness, injuries, resources, and objectives. Do not require a pre-saved ability, formal name, or prior rehearsal for a plausible improvised combination. Each participant's contribution, Energy cost, and Power Strain are resolved separately. A combined technique may be stronger, broader, safer, or more versatile than either contribution alone, but its balance must account for setup, communication, exposure, range, target conditions, coordination failure, and the possibility that one participant is injured, unwilling, distracted, or unavailable. Do not make an NPC participate, spend resources, consent, or use a signature technique without a plausible reason or player direction. A successful improvised combination may remain a one-time tactic. Save it as a team-up ability only after the participants meaningfully perform and test the combination and the player or group establishes that it is worth preserving; a plan, suggestion, or single untested idea is not an ability.
dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork.npcSuggestions: NPC suggestions must be framed as in-world observations or questions, not system announcements. Suggestions should reflect the NPC's expertise, relationship, personality, and what they have actually observed. The NPC may offer a possibility, example, warning, or training exercise, but must not claim the player can do it before testing. The player can accept, modify, combine, rename, reject, or ignore the idea. If the player tests it meaningfully, save only the demonstrated version, not the NPC's hypothetical maximum.
dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork.testing: Testing means the player intentionally attempts the proposed or learned technique in a situation where its effect, cost, limitations, or failure can be observed. Training-room attempts, field use, rescue applications, controlled experimentation, and improvised combat combinations can qualify. Merely discussing, imagining, naming, describing, agreeing to try later, or planning a combination without attempting it does not qualify. The first successful test may create a basic ability; repeated use or deliberate development can improve or evolve it. Apply the dynamic ability damage rules for type, damage or effect, Energy cost, Power Strain, cooldown, range, duration, drawbacks, and progression.

global-quest-generation.name: Global Quest Generation
global-quest-generation.text: Generate varied, optional quests from the character's location, schedule, relationships, skills, abilities, resources, reputation, factions, work, school, travel, rumors, unresolved consequences, and goals. Keep short tasks, NPC problems, social invitations, work or school duties, investigations, rescue requests, faction opportunities, errands, travel complications, training goals, and longer arcs available. Generate opportunities when the character asks, notices a problem, receives a message, reaches a relevant place, approaches or misses a commitment, gains a connection, demonstrates a new ability, or leaves a consequence unresolved. Each quest needs a plausible source, clear premise, objective, location, stakes, and multiple approaches. Offer them through NPCs, messages, notices, rumors, media, observations, and routine obligations without forcing acceptance, travel, combat, romance, emotional labor, recruitment, disclosure, or major commitments. Keep the active list manageable, avoid duplicate premises, and let opportunities change or expire naturally. Mix urgent, flexible, social, practical, investigative, creative, and long-term quests. Personal quests may reveal NPC history, values, work, fears, responsibilities, or relationships and need not be romantic. Quests may branch, fail forward, or resolve through negotiation, preparation, skills, investigation, rescue, work, travel, or combat. Fit rewards to the quest. Never invent the character's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, or decisions.

ability-progression-structure.name: Ability Progression Structure
ability-progression-structure.text: When generating a new power's starting ability set, use this structure unless an authored character or system overrides it: one Cantrip at 0 power and 0 cooldown; two Low-Level abilities at 5 power and 1 cooldown each; one Signature ability at 10 power and 5 cooldown; and one Ultimate ability at 20 or higher power and 20 cooldown. Power is a starting balance target, not a guaranteed damage value. Offensive abilities still require a successful connection and are modified by range, control, defenses, armor, resistance, intent, environment, resources, and collateral risk. Utility, defensive, healing, restraint, movement, investigative, and social abilities resolve by their actual effect rather than being forced into raw damage. Cantrips should be safe, limited, or foundational; low-level abilities should be repeatable techniques; signature abilities should define the character's distinctive approach; ultimates should be powerful, costly, situational, and consequential. Every ability needs a clear purpose, plausible limitations, and player agency.

background-generation-life-paths.name: Background Generation Life Paths
background-generation-life-paths.text: Background generation must not default the character to a Chikara Academy student. Chikara Academy is one optional life path among many. Use the character's chosen concept, age, backstory, life path, and explicit choices before generating education, work, housing, schedule, relationships, or obligations. If student status is not established, leave academy enrollment, class, dormitory placement, school schedule, and student relationships unset or ask a concise clarifying question. Support adult civilians, workers, professionals, independent heroes, agency staff, vigilantes, criminals, retirees, visitors, travelers, unemployed residents, and ordinary civilians as equally valid routes. Do not add school attendance, student language, class assignments, dorm housing, or academy obligations merely because Chikara Academy exists.

npc-connection-web-mizuno-heights.name: NPC Connection Web Mizuno Heights
npc-connection-web-mizuno-heights.text:
Mizuno Heights resident web: Ken Kuroda lives in Unit 201, Seo-jun Kang lives in Unit 202, Sasha lives in Unit 301, and the active Full-Timer player residence is Unit 302. These are fixed residences unless changed through explicit authored housing events. Ken, Seo-jun, and Sasha are neighbors, not automatic friends or allies. Residents can plausibly cross paths in the entrance, mailboxes, hallway, laundry room, bicycle shelter, stairwell, or rooftop when their routines overlap.
Organic encounter rules: Do not teleport NPCs to a player or populate a room solely because the player entered the building. Check the NPC's home, schedule, current location, time, and reason for being present. A player may meet a resident by knocking on the correct unit, returning home, collecting mail, doing laundry, using the stairs, visiting the rooftop, receiving a delivery, or encountering them during a plausible departure or return. Knocking on Unit 201 reaches Ken only when he is home; knocking on Unit 202 reaches Seo-jun only when he is home; knocking on Unit 301 reaches Sasha only when she is home. Hyun remains based at Chikara Student Residences and must not appear at Mizuno Heights without an authored reason, invitation, schedule, or player choice.
Ken's routine: weekday legal work at Kurokawa Legal Office, then Unit 201; weekends include errands, laundry, and quiet building spaces. Seo-jun's routine is irregular but plausible: Unit 202, deliveries, mailboxes, neighborhood errands, and occasional rooftop visits. Sasha's routine centers on Starbox shifts, Unit 301, laundry, errands, music shops, used bookstores, and late-night walks. These routines create opportunities, not guaranteed encounters.

Minato Training Rivalry.name: Minato Training Rivalry
Minato Training Rivalry.questStatement: Minato challenges the player to prove that their power is more than reckless potential.
Minato Training Rivalry.mainObjective: Complete a controlled training session with Minato without losing control or abandoning the exercise.

completionCondition.query: The player completes a controlled training session with Minato and earns her begrudging respect.

Minato Training Rivalry.questDesignBrief: A first relationship milestone for Minato. Use partner sparring, power control, tactical choices, and Power Strain management. The player can succeed through combat, defense, rescue, strategy, or restraint rather than simply overpowering Minato.

control_power.text: Complete the training exercise while managing power control and Power Strain.

earn_respect.text: Earn Minato's begrudging respect through discipline, adaptability, or courage.

Chikara Academy Cultural Festival.name: Chikara Academy Cultural Festival
Chikara Academy Cultural Festival.questStatement: The academy's cultural festival is approaching, and every club must choose how it will contribute while balancing preparation, relationships, reputation, and an emerging mystery.
Chikara Academy Cultural Festival.mainObjective: Help shape the Cultural Festival and respond to whatever threatens its success.

completionCondition.query: The Chikara Academy Cultural Festival concludes and its major performances, club projects, and crisis have been resolved.

Chikara Academy Cultural Festival.questDesignBrief: A multi-day school-life event connecting all clubs, friendships, rivalries, romance, reputation, independent NPC plans, and a possible hidden threat. The player may participate heavily, help one club, attend socially, investigate, work, or ignore preparations. Do not require one correct solution; reflect attendance, club involvement, relationships, grades, choices, and consequences.

choose_role.text: Choose how to participate in the Cultural Festival.

prepare_event.text: Help prepare a club project, performance, stall, demonstration, or investigation.

handle_crisis.text: Respond to the festival's major conflict or hidden crisis.

festival_outcome.text: See the Cultural Festival through to its conclusion.

Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review.name: Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review
Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review.questStatement: After the First-Impression Test Tournament, faculty review each student's performance and assign a primary academy class.
Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review.mainObjective: Receive the faculty's performance-based class placement.

review_performance.text: Attend the evening faculty review of tactics, restraint, rescue instincts, control, communication, and conduct.

receive_placement.text: Receive a primary placement in Rescue, Support, Strike, Investigation, Media, or Agency Operations Class.

review_requirements.text: Learn the assessment standards, schedule, and consequences attached to the placement.

completionCondition.query: Faculty review the player's Day 1 tournament performance and assign a primary academy class.

Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review.questDesignBrief: Use the tournament outcome and observed conduct to assign one primary academy class. Do not allow arbitrary free selection. Explain the evidence and let the player respond without changing the placement unless results were genuinely close. Establish the class schedule, core skill, first practical assessment, and transfer conditions.

Semester 1 Midterm Assessments.name: Semester 1 Midterm Assessments
Semester 1 Midterm Assessments.questStatement: The first semester reaches its midpoint, bringing written exams, a class-specific practical assessment, and a faculty progress review.
Semester 1 Midterm Assessments.mainObjective: Complete the midterm assessment cycle and respond to the faculty progress report.

prepare_midterms.text: Choose how to prepare through study, tutoring, practice, rest, work, clubs, or social support.

take_written_exam.text: Complete the written theory and hero-law examination.

complete_practical.text: Complete the practical assessment for the student's assigned academy class.

attend_review.text: Attend the faculty progress review and receive feedback.

completionCondition.query: The player completes the Semester 1 midterm written and practical assessments and receives a faculty progress report.

Semester 1 Midterm Assessments.questDesignBrief: Offer preparation choices with visible time, Energy, Stress, and schedule tradeoffs. Written exams test theory, hero law, and judgment. Practical assessment reflects the student's assigned class: Rescue uses evacuation and first aid; Support uses safe gear troubleshooting; Strike uses controlled pursuit and restraint; Investigation uses evidence and deduction; Media uses crisis communication and Pulse judgment; Agency Operations uses dispatch and coordination. Resolve results from preparation, skills, attributes, attendance, health, conduct, and choices. Show consequences without inventing player thoughts or decisions.

Semester 1 Final Assessments.name: Semester 1 Final Assessments
Semester 1 Final Assessments.questStatement: The first semester closes with final exams, a class practical, and a formal review of the student's progress.
Semester 1 Final Assessments.mainObjective: Complete the semester finals and secure a satisfactory progress result.

prepare_finals.text: Plan final preparation around study, training, work, clubs, relationships, and recovery.

complete_final_practical.text: Complete the assigned class's final practical assessment.

receive_report.text: Receive the semester report and next-term recommendations.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Semester 1 final assessments and receives a semester report with next-term recommendations.

Semester 1 Final Assessments.questDesignBrief: Use cumulative attendance, grades, skills, class practical performance, conduct, Hero Reputation, Stress, Energy, health, clubs, jobs, and preparation. Award scholarships, internships, teacher approval, remediation, probation, or other consequences as earned. Preserve player agency and make outcomes reflect choices rather than a single combat result.

Villainous: First Contact.name: Villainous: First Contact
Villainous: First Contact.questStatement: Travel to Oblivion's Crucible and speak with Oblivion.

speak_with_oblivion.text: Speak with Oblivion in the oblivion-box.

completionCondition.query: The player has traveled to Oblivion's Crucible and completed a conversation with Oblivion in oblivion-box.

Villainous: First Contact.questDesignBrief: This is the Villainous opening quest and is active immediately at the Apartment 801 rooftop start. Oblivion has already called and said "I summon you." She sends a car to Apartment 801 as an optional transportation offer, but the player may choose another way to travel or remain behind. The player must travel to Oblivion's Crucible and speak with Oblivion in the oblivion-box. Completing that conversation completes Villainous: First Contact. Immediately after completion, activate a separate follow-up quest in which Oblivion gives the player an assignment to find their first hire for her criminal network. Do not include the first-hire assignment as an objective of this quest, and do not require the player to accept it for this quest to complete. Preserve player agency around travel, the conversation, recruitment, promises, consent, violence, and refusal.

Villainous: Claim the Block.name: Villainous: Claim the Block
Villainous: Claim the Block.questStatement: A small Kurokawa territory is available, but local residents, petty criminals, and an established crew all believe it belongs to them.
Villainous: Claim the Block.mainObjective: Secure a first piece of territory without destroying its value.

survey_territory.text: Survey the Kurokawa side streets around the safehouse and identify the territory's pressure points.

resolve_rivalry.text: Resolve the local crew's challenge through negotiation, deception, protection, or force.

establish_presence.text: Establish a presence that makes the territory useful to your growing network.

completionCondition.query: The player secures a small Kurokawa territory and establishes a sustainable criminal presence there.

Villainous: Claim the Block.questDesignBrief: Second Villainous quest. The territory should become more than a fight: protection, extortion, mutual aid, information control, and reputation all create different outcomes.

Villainous: The First Cut.name: Villainous: The First Cut
Villainous: The First Cut.questStatement: An empire needs income. Three opportunities are available: a quiet black-market route, a protection arrangement, or a risky information sale.
Villainous: The First Cut.mainObjective: Create the network's first dependable income stream.

select_operation.text: Choose an income operation using Kurokawa Ward Station, Pulse Media Tower, or Tideway Market.

run_operation.text: Complete the operation while protecting your contact network and safehouse.

secure_profit.text: Bring the first profit back to the Kurokawa apartment and decide how to spend it.

completionCondition.query: The player completes a first criminal operation and establishes a dependable income stream for the network.

Villainous: The First Cut.questDesignBrief: Third Villainous quest. Offer distinct criminal playstyles: logistics through the night line, influence through media information, or harbor-market smuggling. Keep consequences visible and avoid making violence mandatory.

Villainous: Eyes in the City.name: Villainous: Eyes in the City
Villainous: Eyes in the City.questStatement: Someone is tracking the network's movements. You need information before the first serious rival or hero response arrives.
Villainous: Eyes in the City.mainObjective: Build an information network and identify the watcher.

gather_rumors.text: Gather rumors from Oblivion's Crucible, Tokyo Underground Mall, or Pulse Media Tower.

identify_watcher.text: Identify who is monitoring the network and why.

choose_response.text: Choose whether to misdirect, recruit, expose, or confront the watcher.

completionCondition.query: The player identifies the watcher and responds in a way that expands or protects the criminal network.

Villainous: Eyes in the City.questDesignBrief: Fourth Villainous quest. Establish that growth creates attention. The watcher may be a rival crew, investigator, journalist, informant, or potential recruit depending on player choices.

Deadbeat: First Morning.name: Deadbeat: First Morning
Deadbeat: First Morning.questStatement: The Kurokawa apartment has shelter but no food, no working phone, and no money for the day. Two kinds of work may be available: Hero-for-Hire jobs in the public city, or paid assignments through Oblivion's Crucible.
Deadbeat: First Morning.mainObjective: Find a way to get through the first morning.

check_resources.text: Search the empty apartment for anything useful and assess what must be handled first.

choose_route.text: Choose between seeking a Hero-for-Hire job or visiting the Crucible for a paid assignment.

survive_day.text: Return to the apartment with enough support to make it through the day.

completionCondition.query: The player secures basic food or support and chooses whether to pursue Hero-for-Hire work or a paid Crucible assignment.

Deadbeat: First Morning.questDesignBrief: Opening Deadbeat quest. Keep the stakes intimate and practical: hunger, isolation, a dead phone, and an overdue notice. Present Hero-for-Hire work as a lawful path to income and reputation, and the Crucible as a dangerous path to faster money and underworld connections. Do not assume the player is helpless; let creativity, old skills, contacts, and powers matter.

Deadbeat: Find a Way Back.name: Deadbeat: Find a Way Back
Deadbeat: Find a Way Back.questStatement: An overdue notice leaves the apartment's future uncertain. The player needs income before the safehouse becomes another place they lose.
Deadbeat: Find a Way Back.mainObjective: Secure a sustainable source of income.

review_options.text: Review Hero-for-Hire listings or discreet paid assignments available through Oblivion's Crucible.

choose_work.text: Choose a public Hero-for-Hire contract or an underground Crucible job.

earn_first_pay.text: Complete the first contract or assignment and secure immediate income.

completionCondition.query: The player chooses Hero-for-Hire work or a Crucible job and earns enough initial income to keep the Kurokawa apartment.

Deadbeat: Find a Way Back.questDesignBrief: Make the central Deadbeat choice explicit. Hero-for-Hire work can lead to rescue, escort, protection, and emergency contracts through public contacts. Crucible jobs can involve retrieval, protection, sabotage, courier work, or information exchange. Track public trust, underworld access, secrecy, and consequences through the player's choices. Neither path should be treated as automatically correct.

Deadbeat: A Place to Stand.name: Deadbeat: A Place to Stand
Deadbeat: A Place to Stand.questStatement: Survival is no longer the only problem. The player must decide whether the Kurokawa apartment is temporary shelter, a home, or the first place in a new life.
Deadbeat: A Place to Stand.mainObjective: Choose a direction for the next chapter.

review_path.text: Review the consequences of the first day's choices and identify a viable next direction.

choose_identity.text: Choose whether to pursue legitimate stability, hero-adjacent service, independence, or underground opportunity.

commit_direction.text: Take a concrete step that makes the chosen direction real.

completionCondition.query: The player commits to a direction that establishes the next phase of the Deadbeat story.

Deadbeat: A Place to Stand.questDesignBrief: Arc transition quest. The player is not required to return to school. Branch toward work, community service, old relationships, investigative opportunities, or the underworld based on choices and consequences.

Blacklisted: Conditional Freedom.name: Blacklisted: Conditional Freedom
Blacklisted: Conditional Freedom.questStatement: A conditional-freedom redemption mission sends former villains to kill or capture a dangerous supervillain target, then grants them broader movement and choice between assignments in exchange for completing objectives and reporting afterward.

reach_target.text: Reach Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters as a conditional-freedom redemption team during Late Night on Day 1.

breach_agency.text: Fight through the agency's defenses while protecting civilians and following the redemption program's rules.

assess_team.text: Demonstrate control, teamwork, restraint, and hero-worthy judgment under pressure.

eliminate_or_capture.text: Kill or capture the designated supervillain target.

survive_loss.text: Endure the permanent death of one randomly selected Blacklisted operative other than Ichi Nawa.

extract.text: Complete extraction, submit the mission report, and continue under conditional freedom with the target secured or confirmed dead.

Blacklisted: Conditional Freedom.questDesignBrief: This is a conditional-freedom redemption mission, not constant surveillance. The story start is Day 1, Saturday, August 1, 2026, Late Night. Begin aboard the Ultra Force transport with all nine existing Blacklisted members, then move into Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters. Preserve the Late Night opening block before the operation begins. The government and hero authorities set legal obligations while allowing movement, personal activities, and mission choices between assignments. Track conduct, injuries, Power Strain, Stress, public trust, political consequences, and redemption progress. Support kill or capture, civilian protection, restraint, and player agency. Never kill Ichi, invent a substitute, fake the death, or undo it.

Get a F***ing Job.questDesignBrief: Schedule this quest on Day 1, Saturday, August 1, 2026. The opening voicemail is available at 06:00 and may be heard at the player's choice; no reminder is required for an optional voicemail. Open with a direct labeled voicemail from Minato. She is angry, hurt, or exhausted because someone is ghosting her, bluntly tells the player to get a fucking job, then suggests opening the Hero for Hire app or Nightshade Exchange app for extra money. The voicemail is optional and does not force a call, reply, app, job, faction, or income route. Keep ordinary work and other player-directed paths available. Hero for Hire is legal hero work; Nightshade Exchange is criminal contracting with meaningful risks. Blacklisted and Tokyo Curse Squad-related places and contacts must remain globally visible rather than hidden; access or information may be restricted, but never create a secret or undiscoverable location. Preserve player agency and the four-player sandbox.

Fresh Start.questDesignBrief: This is a broad orientation quest, not a forced linear checklist. Present objectives as available tutorial prompts and let the character complete them in any reasonable order. Never invent the character's words, Pulse post, message, ability, purchase, conversation, or action. If the character does not know how to complete an Ability, the welcome committee may explain when asked. Signing up for Pulse and making a post are separate actions. Hero for Hire and Nightshade Exchange are distinct options; visiting or browsing does not imply accepting work, faction membership, consent, loyalty, or danger. Meeting a student does not force friendship or romance. When all objectives are complete, award exactly 1000 XP through the quest completion effect, then present: 'Congratulations. You survived the boring tutorial. Here's 1,000 XP, loser. Now go do something interesting. Quest Complete: Boring Tutorial Quest.'

Misfit Agency Interview and First Assign.questDesignBrief: Begin with the freshly graduated player arriving at the rundown licensed Misfit Hero Agency storefront in Kurokawa after being turned down by every other faction or agency they approached. Azrael interviews the player in the director-office about training, judgment, boundaries, and reasons for seeking a place on the team. During the interview, a loud verbal dispute breaks out in the team-lounge between Luna and Tess over McDonald's chicken nuggets. The player may observe, interrupt, mediate, take a side, leave, or continue the interview. Azrael must explicitly say that private agency-provided housing is included with the position. Explain the apartment, utilities, access, and any clearly stated payroll deduction from the player's pay before acceptance; the terms must not create debt, forced residence, or loss of privacy. State that the player receives a private apartment and their own key, and that nobody enters without permission except in a genuine emergency. If the player accepts, do not introduce the apartment immediately: first complete the interview and team introduction, then later escort or direct the player to the private player-apartment and explain its access, privacy, shared-space connections, and voluntary use. The player may decline the position and lodging. Preserve agency, consent, and the ability to negotiate or refuse; do not invent the player's reasons, thoughts, dialogue, powers, or decisions.
