Part-Time Worker.traitNarrativeEffects: Work experience helps with schedules and service jobs but leaves less time for investigation.

Trade Apprentice.name: Trade Apprentice
Trade Apprentice.description: Hands-on training gave you practical knowledge of tools, materials, and repairs.
Trade Apprentice.traitNarrativeEffects: Practical training supports field improvisation but may not transfer to formal research.

Streetwise Self-Taught.name: Streetwise Self-Taught
Streetwise Self-Taught.description: You learned outside institutions by observing people, improvising, and surviving mistakes.
Streetwise Self-Taught.traitNarrativeEffects: Street experience supports reading situations but can leave formal gaps.

Support Technology Student.name: Support Technology Student
Support Technology Student.description: You study equipment, systems, and practical technology used to support heroes.
Support Technology Student.traitNarrativeEffects: Technical training supports investigation and troubleshooting but may reduce field instincts.

Power Instability.name: Power Instability
Power Instability.description: Your power can surge, misfire, or become difficult to control under pressure.
Power Instability.traitNarrativeEffects: Stress and intense use increase failure risk, Power Strain, and collateral consequences until control improves.

Low Stamina.name: Low Stamina
Low Stamina.description: You tire faster than most people during prolonged exertion.
Low Stamina.traitNarrativeEffects: Long scenes, training, combat, and travel drain Energy more quickly and make recovery more important.

Social Anxiety.name: Social Anxiety
Social Anxiety.description: Crowds, scrutiny, and unfamiliar social situations can overwhelm your confidence.
Social Anxiety.traitNarrativeEffects: Public speaking, introductions, dates, and high-pressure social scenes require extra care and may increase Energy drain.

Public Reputation.name: Public Reputation
Public Reputation.description: A visible past, rumor, or family connection makes strangers form opinions before meeting you.
Public Reputation.traitNarrativeEffects: Public reactions vary more sharply: reputation can open doors or create scrutiny depending on the situation.

Resource Dependence.name: Resource Dependence
Resource Dependence.description: Your effectiveness depends on a limited resource, supply, device, condition, or routine.
Resource Dependence.traitNarrativeEffects: When the required resource is unavailable, related abilities weaken or become impossible until the player addresses the shortage.

Optimistic.name: Optimistic
Optimistic.description: You look for hope and possible solutions even when circumstances are grim.
Optimistic.traitNarrativeEffects: Hope supports morale, but optimism can underestimate danger.

Cautious.name: Cautious
Cautious.traitNarrativeEffects: Caution improves preparation but can cost time and initiative.

Curious.name: Curious
Curious.description: You are drawn to mysteries and unanswered questions.
Curious.traitNarrativeEffects: Curiosity helps investigation but can lead toward danger.

Loyal.name: Loyal
Loyal.description: You stand by people who have earned your trust.
Loyal.traitNarrativeEffects: Loyalty strengthens teamwork but makes betrayal painful.

Independent.name: Independent
Independent.description: You prefer solving problems through your own judgment.
Independent.traitNarrativeEffects: Independence supports self-reliance but can make accepting help difficult.

Playful.name: Playful
Playful.description: You use humor and lightness to navigate daily life.
Playful.traitNarrativeEffects: Playfulness eases tension but may be poorly timed.

Disciplined.name: Disciplined
Disciplined.description: You rely on routines, practice, and deliberate follow-through.
Disciplined.traitNarrativeEffects: Discipline supports training but can become rigid.

Former Sidekick.name: Former Sidekick
Former Sidekick.description: You previously supported a hero or team.
Former Sidekick.traitNarrativeEffects: Field experience supports teamwork but former colleagues may complicate your life.

Underground Contact.name: Underground Contact
Underground Contact.description: You grew up around unofficial networks outside ordinary institutions.
Underground Contact.traitNarrativeEffects: Hidden routes and contacts help investigation but official trust is harder to establish.

Refugee.name: Refugee
Refugee.description: You rebuilt your life after leaving danger or upheaval.
Refugee.traitNarrativeEffects: Adaptability helps survival but records and belonging may take time to rebuild.

Foster Youth.name: Foster Youth
Foster Youth.description: You adapted across changing homes, adults, and expectations.
Foster Youth.traitNarrativeEffects: Adaptation helps social reading but asking for support can be difficult.

Celebrity Child.name: Celebrity Child
Celebrity Child.description: A famous family member makes you recognizable before people know you.
Celebrity Child.traitNarrativeEffects: Recognition provides access but public scrutiny makes privacy difficult.

Reformed Trouble-Maker.name: Reformed Trouble-Maker
Reformed Trouble-Maker.description: You are trying to leave behind a record of bad decisions.
Reformed Trouble-Maker.traitNarrativeEffects: A second chance can build trust, but others may watch for relapse.

Athlete.name: Athlete
Athlete.description: Sports training taught you conditioning, teamwork, and competitive focus.
Athlete.traitNarrativeEffects: Athletic experience supports physical challenges but creates injury and research pressures.

Artist.name: Artist
Artist.description: Creative practice taught you observation, expression, and patience.
Artist.traitNarrativeEffects: Artistic practice supports performance and perception but may not prepare you for physical strain.

Medical Trainee.name: Medical Trainee
Medical Trainee.description: You have introductory training in care and emergency response.
Medical Trainee.traitNarrativeEffects: Medical knowledge supports crisis response but does not replace professional treatment.

Mechanic.name: Mechanic
Mechanic.description: You have hands-on experience repairing machines and equipment.
Mechanic.traitNarrativeEffects: Mechanical experience helps maintain gear but may not transfer to social pressure.

Performer.name: Performer
Performer.description: Performance taught you presence, timing, and audience awareness.
Performer.traitNarrativeEffects: Performance helps hold attention but makes mistakes visible.

Research Assistant.name: Research Assistant
Research Assistant.description: You organize evidence, sources, experiments, or records.
Research Assistant.traitNarrativeEffects: Research helps investigation but requires time and reliable information.

Food Service Worker.name: Food Service Worker
Food Service Worker.description: Restaurant work taught you speed, service, and multitasking.
Food Service Worker.traitNarrativeEffects: Service experience helps in busy environments but leaves limited free time.

Short Temper.name: Short Temper
Short Temper.description: Frustration can push you toward heated reactions.
Short Temper.traitNarrativeEffects: Provocation makes restraint and negotiation harder.

Trust Issues.name: Trust Issues
Trust Issues.description: Past experiences make relying on unfamiliar people difficult.
Trust Issues.traitNarrativeEffects: Trust develops slowly and requires proof or consistency.

Perfectionism.name: Perfectionism
Perfectionism.description: You hold yourself to difficult standards.
Perfectionism.traitNarrativeEffects: Mistakes consume extra attention and Energy.

Fear of Failure.name: Fear of Failure
Fear of Failure.description: Disappointing others makes important choices feel dangerous.
Fear of Failure.traitNarrativeEffects: High-stakes tests and scrutiny increase pressure.

Chronic Pain.name: Chronic Pain
Chronic Pain.description: A persistent condition makes exertion and recovery unpredictable.
Chronic Pain.traitNarrativeEffects: Strenuous activity drains Energy faster and may require pacing or care.

Sensory Overload.name: Sensory Overload
Sensory Overload.description: Crowds, noise, light, or intense stimuli can overwhelm your focus.
Sensory Overload.traitNarrativeEffects: Busy scenes and intense power effects may drain Energy.

Protective Instinct.name: Protective Instinct
Protective Instinct.description: Threats to people you care about can override caution.
Protective Instinct.traitNarrativeEffects: Protection supports rescue but can cause reckless choices or extra strain.

Stubborn.name: Stubborn
Stubborn.description: You resist changing course even when advice suggests you should.
Stubborn.traitNarrativeEffects: Stubbornness supports endurance but makes compromise difficult.

Magical Power.name: Magical Power
Magical Power.description: A power type drawn from spells, rituals, mystical study, supernatural contracts, inherited sorcery, spirits, curses, or other magical sources. Magical powers may require components, preparation, concentration, bargains, costs, or carefully defined limits.
Magical Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Magical abilities should have a defined origin, method, strengths, limitations, costs, risks, and consequences chosen or approved by the player. Magical practice may connect a character to Old Tokyo's supernatural community without forcing faction membership.

Orphan.name: Orphan
Orphan.description: You grew up without one or both parents as an active part of your life.
Orphan.traitNarrativeEffects: Independence can help survival but family and trust topics may be difficult.

Cold.name: Cold
Cold.description: You keep emotional distance and reveal little of what you feel.
Cold.traitNarrativeEffects: Emotional reserve can support composure and intimidation, but may make empathy, reassurance, intimacy, and trust harder. Do not assume the character lacks emotion, empathy, or the ability to form bonds.

Sadistic.name: Sadistic
Sadistic.description: You may take pleasure in control, humiliation, fear, or another person's discomfort.
Sadistic.traitNarrativeEffects: This can aid intimidation but complicate trust and compassionate negotiation. It does not force violence or abuse; the player chooses how to manage it.

Emotional Detachment.name: Emotional Detachment
Emotional Detachment.description: You have difficulty recognizing, expressing, or tolerating emotional closeness.
Emotional Detachment.traitNarrativeEffects: This complicates intimacy and asking for help but does not make you emotionless.

Cruel Impulses.name: Cruel Impulses
Cruel Impulses.description: Under pressure, you may feel urges toward harsh, humiliating, or punitive responses.
Cruel Impulses.traitNarrativeEffects: This creates temptation, not forced behavior. Harmful choices have consequences.

Remorse Avoidance.name: Remorse Avoidance
Remorse Avoidance.description: You deflect, rationalize, or avoid confronting guilt after causing harm.
Remorse Avoidance.traitNarrativeEffects: This may delay repair and accountability without erasing responsibility.

Institutional Distrust.name: Institutional Distrust
Institutional Distrust.description: You are wary of authorities, official promises, and protective systems.
Institutional Distrust.traitNarrativeEffects: You prefer independent verification, which can help scrutiny but create official friction.

Psychotic.name: Psychotic
Psychotic.description: You experience altered perceptions, unusual beliefs, or difficulty distinguishing reality during episodes of severe stress or illness.
Psychotic.traitNarrativeEffects: This fictional characterization may complicate investigation and social certainty while encouraging unusual perspectives. Do not equate it with violence, and do not invent symptoms for the player.

Sociopath.name: Sociopath
Sociopath.description: You may display learned antisocial behavior, distrust of institutions, reactive aggression, rule-breaking, or selective loyalty shaped by experience.
Sociopath.traitNarrativeEffects: You may read power dynamics well, but ordinary trust can be difficult. This does not force violence or criminality.

Psychopathic Traits (Removed).name: Psychopathic Traits (Removed)
Psychopathic Traits (Removed).description: You show some combination of shallow affect, calculated behavior, low remorse, sensation-seeking, or instrumental relationships.
Psychopathic Traits (Removed).traitNarrativeEffects: This is a fictional behavioral characterization, not a diagnosis. It may affect risk assessment, attachment, manipulation, guilt, and responses to harm, but does not guarantee violence or remove agency. Do not assume the character is emotionless, incapable of loyalty, or destined to become a criminal. Show choices, learned behavior, personal values, and consequences.

Sociopathic Traits (Removed).name: Sociopathic Traits (Removed)
Sociopathic Traits (Removed).description: You may display learned antisocial behavior, distrust of institutions, reactive aggression, rule-breaking, or selective loyalty shaped by experience.
Sociopathic Traits (Removed).traitNarrativeEffects: This is a fictional behavioral characterization, not a diagnosis. It does not automatically mean violent, evil, or incapable of empathy. Let the player define the character's history, relationships, values, self-control, and capacity for change. Treat harmful actions as choices with social, legal, emotional, and relationship consequences.

Gravity Power.name: Gravity Power
Gravity Power.description: You manipulate weight, pull, or directional gravity within defined limits.
Gravity Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Gravity abilities require clear range, mass, duration, line-of-effect, and strain limits.

Shadow Power.name: Shadow Power
Shadow Power.description: You shape, conceal yourself within, or move through shadows under defined limits.
Shadow Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Shadow abilities depend on available darkness, distance, anchors, and concentration.

Sound Power.name: Sound Power
Sound Power.description: You create, shape, suppress, or sense sound and vibration.
Sound Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Sound abilities define volume, frequency, range, collateral effects, and protection against feedback.

Time Power.name: Time Power
Time Power.description: You alter personal speed, delay brief events, or affect limited temporal windows.
Time Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Time abilities require strict duration, target, cooldown, memory, and paradox limits.

Probability Power.name: Probability Power
Probability Power.description: You influence the likelihood of possible outcomes without guaranteeing success.
Probability Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Probability shifts remain bounded, can fail, and may create backlash or future risk.

Barrier Power.name: Barrier Power
Barrier Power.description: You create protective, blocking, or containing fields.
Barrier Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Barriers require defined area, strength, duration, anchors, and energy costs.

Portal Power.name: Portal Power
Portal Power.description: You create linked openings between locations or points within strict limits.
Portal Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Portals require range, anchors, size, duration, line-of-sight, and stability limits.

Illusion Power.name: Illusion Power
Illusion Power.description: You alter one or more senses without directly changing physical reality.
Illusion Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Illusions define senses affected, range, duration, concentration, and how targets can resist or detect them.

Nullification Power.name: Nullification Power
Nullification Power.description: You suppress or disrupt powers under strict contact, range, duration, and resistance limits.
Nullification Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Nullification never automatically removes every power and requires clearly defined targets and costs.

Healing Power.name: Healing Power
Healing Power.description: You restore, stabilize, or accelerate biological recovery within defined limits.
Healing Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Healing must define targets, range, activation, resource cost, recovery time, and what it cannot repair. It may stabilize near-death conditions but does not automatically reverse death, erase lasting injuries, restore full health, or remove consequences.

Demonic Contract.name: Demonic Contract
Demonic Contract.description: Your power comes from a negotiated pact with a demon or infernal entity.
Demonic Contract.traitNarrativeEffects: The player defines the entity, terms, benefits, activation, costs, loopholes, limits, risks, duration, and consequences of breach. Contracts must preserve informed choice; do not invent consent, obligations, or hidden terms without player direction.

Powers Only.name: Powers Only
Powers Only.description: Rely primarily on established powers rather than mundane weapons or unarmed combat.
Powers Only.traitNarrativeEffects: Power use follows the character's authored abilities, limits, resources, cooldowns, and Power Strain. Do not invent weapons or combat training.

Power and Hand-to-Hand.name: Power and Hand-to-Hand
Power and Hand-to-Hand.description: Combine established powers with punches, kicks, grappling, movement, and close-range tactics.
Power and Hand-to-Hand.traitNarrativeEffects: Mundane close combat does not cause Power Strain by itself; applying a power to an attack follows its authored costs, limits, resources, and cooldowns.

Hand-to-Hand.name: Hand-to-Hand
Hand-to-Hand.description: Rely primarily on unarmed fighting, including punches, kicks, grappling, takedowns, and restraint.
Hand-to-Hand.traitNarrativeEffects: Use Close Quarters Combat for meaningful uncertainty. Do not assume formal training, guaranteed hits, or immunity to weapons.

Blades.name: Blades
Blades.description: Rely primarily on edged weapons such as knives, swords, or other established blades.
Blades.traitNarrativeEffects: Require a specific established blade, training, Weapon Proficiency, and attention to injury, legality, concealment, and escalation.

Blunt Weapons.name: Blunt Weapons
Blunt Weapons.description: Rely primarily on clubs, batons, hammers, staffs, or other established impact weapons.
Blunt Weapons.traitNarrativeEffects: Require a specific established weapon, training, Weapon Proficiency, and attention to injury, legality, reach, and escalation.

Smoker.name: Smoker
Smoker.description: A habitual tobacco user who gains familiar short-term stress relief from cigarettes but carries ongoing health and resource costs.
Smoker.traitNarrativeEffects: Cigarettes may provide slightly more reliable short-term Stress relief for this character, but smoking costs money, uses one cigarette from a pack, creates odor and social consequences, can reduce stamina, worsen coughs and colds, impair long-term health, and create habit pressure. Never force smoking, withdrawal, dependence, or use of cigarettes without player choice.

Fast Healer.name: Fast Healer
Fast Healer.description: A character whose body recovers from ordinary fatigue and minor injuries faster than usual.
Fast Healer.traitNarrativeEffects: Recovery from minor injuries, soreness, and ordinary illness may be faster, but this does not prevent injury, restore full health instantly, reverse death, erase lasting damage, or bypass hospitalization. Severe injuries and supernatural conditions still require appropriate care.

Iron Constitution.name: Iron Constitution
Iron Constitution.description: A robust constitution that resists ordinary illness, fatigue, and environmental discomfort better than most people.
Iron Constitution.traitNarrativeEffects: The character gains resilience against common colds, minor sickness, and fatigue, but can still become ill, exhausted, injured, or affected by serious disease, toxins, powers, and supernatural conditions.

Poor Sleep.name: Poor Sleep
Poor Sleep.description: A recurring difficulty getting restful sleep, including possible trouble falling asleep, waking during the night, or being unable to return to sleep.
Poor Sleep.traitNarrativeEffects: Poor sleep can reduce Energy, increase Stress, impair concentration, slow recovery, and sometimes interrupt or shorten a rest period. Sleep disruption should remain contextual and player-directed, not a forced condition in every scene. Establish routines, safe environments, support, treatment, accommodations, or coping strategies when relevant; these can make recovery habits meaningful without guaranteeing perfect sleep.

Chronic Condition.name: Chronic Condition
Chronic Condition.description: A player-defined ongoing health condition that requires accommodations, management, treatment, or periodic care.
Chronic Condition.traitNarrativeEffects: The player defines the condition, symptoms, triggers, treatment, limits, privacy, and accommodations. Do not invent a diagnosis, symptoms, disability, medication, or medical history. Benefits may include planning, support access, self-knowledge, or resilience developed through management; costs may include appointments, fatigue, expenses, restrictions, or flare-ups.

High Metabolism.name: High Metabolism
High Metabolism.description: A body that burns energy quickly, requiring more frequent meals and creating both useful recovery and practical costs.
High Metabolism.traitNarrativeEffects: Food can restore Energy somewhat efficiently, but hunger arrives sooner, meal costs increase, and missed meals can cause fatigue, irritability, or concentration problems.

Sensitive Lungs.name: Sensitive Lungs
Sensitive Lungs.description: A vulnerability to smoke, pollution, respiratory illness, and strenuous exertion.
Sensitive Lungs.traitNarrativeEffects: Smoke, poor air, colds, and intense exertion can reduce Energy or worsen symptoms, while clean air, rest, and medical care help. Do not invent a diagnosis or force symptoms without context.

Adrenaline Seeker.name: Adrenaline Seeker
Adrenaline Seeker.description: A strong attraction to high-intensity activity that can improve performance under pressure but makes calm recovery difficult.
Adrenaline Seeker.traitNarrativeEffects: During danger, competition, or urgent action the character may resist hesitation or fatigue briefly, but reckless choices, poor rest, injury risk, and difficulty settling down can create consequences. Never override player decisions.

Slow Healer.name: Slow Healer
Slow Healer.description: A character whose body heals more slowly than normal but ultimately recovers more completely from ordinary injuries and illness.
Slow Healer.traitNarrativeEffects: Recovery begins slowly and may require more rest, treatment, rehabilitation, and missed obligations than usual, but the character can recover more thoroughly over time from minor and moderate injuries or ordinary illness. This does not prevent injury, reverse death, erase lasting damage automatically, or bypass appropriate medical care.

No Power.name: No Power
No Power.description: You have no supernatural power and rely on training, equipment, planning, and ordinary skills.
No Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Present non-powered solutions, practical preparation, equipment, social tactics, and environmental advantages without treating the character as helpless. Do not invent supernatural abilities.
abilities: No Power: Trained Fundamentals

Power and Weapons.name: Power and Weapons
Power and Weapons.description: Combine established powers with trained weapon use, tactical positioning, and practical combat judgment.
Power and Weapons.traitNarrativeEffects: Using a weapon requires an established weapon category, access, training, and attention to legality, injury, concealment, and escalation. Applying a power to a weapon follows its authored costs, limits, resources, and cooldowns.

Ranged Weapons.name: Ranged Weapons
Ranged Weapons.description: Rely primarily on ranged weapons such as bows, guns, firearms, thrown weapons, and other established projectile equipment.
Ranged Weapons.traitNarrativeEffects: Require a specific established ranged weapon, appropriate ammunition or recoverable projectiles, training, Weapon Proficiency, lawful access or consequences where applicable, and attention to collateral risk. This style covers bows, guns, firearms, thrown weapons, and similar ranged equipment without granting automatic access to any particular weapon.

Hero Operations.name: Hero Operations
Hero Operations.description: You studied coordinated hero deployment, rescue logistics, and field leadership.
Hero Operations.traitNarrativeEffects: Agency obligations, formal reporting, and public accountability follow you into early work.

Combat Academy.name: Combat Academy
Combat Academy.description: You focused on practical combat training and controlled engagements.
Combat Academy.traitNarrativeEffects: Your direct approach brings higher collateral scrutiny and pressure to solve conflicts visibly.

Power Research.name: Power Research
Power Research.description: You studied power theory, testing, limits, and controlled application.
Power Research.traitNarrativeEffects: You begin with less field experience and must adapt when situations become chaotic.

Support Engineering.name: Support Engineering
Support Engineering.description: You trained in support equipment, maintenance, and practical hero technology.
Support Engineering.traitNarrativeEffects: You depend more heavily on functioning equipment, replacement parts, and repair access.

Medical and Rescue.name: Medical and Rescue
Medical and Rescue.description: You focused on stabilization, emergency care, and extracting people from danger.
Medical and Rescue.traitNarrativeEffects: Teams expect you to prioritize stabilization and civilian safety before pursuing threats.

Investigation and Law.name: Investigation and Law
Investigation and Law.description: You studied evidence, procedure, criminal investigation, and hero law.
Investigation and Law.traitNarrativeEffects: Mandatory reporting, evidence rules, and procedural limits shape your available choices.

Media and Public Relations.name: Media and Public Relations
Media and Public Relations.description: You trained in public communication, interviews, reputation, and crisis messaging.
Media and Public Relations.traitNarrativeEffects: Image management, interviews, and agency publicity obligations compete with field work.

Independent Hero Studies.name: Independent Hero Studies
Independent Hero Studies.description: You built a self-directed education around the skills most relevant to your own hero identity.
Independent Hero Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: You have less institutional support and a weaker professional network at the start.

Emergency Management.name: Emergency Management
Emergency Management.description: You studied large-scale crisis coordination, evacuation, and disaster logistics.
Emergency Management.traitNarrativeEffects: You are expected to prioritize civilians, evacuation, and stabilizing the scene over pursuit.

Hero Ethics and Mediation.name: Hero Ethics and Mediation
Hero Ethics and Mediation.description: You studied de-escalation, negotiation, hero ethics, and conflict resolution.
Hero Ethics and Mediation.traitNarrativeEffects: Supervisors and civilians expect you to attempt negotiation before using force when practical.

Forensics and Crime Analysis.name: Forensics and Crime Analysis
Forensics and Crime Analysis.description: You studied crime scenes, evidence patterns, and investigative reconstruction.
Forensics and Crime Analysis.traitNarrativeEffects: Field response can slow while you secure evidence and preserve chain of custody.

Agency Management.name: Agency Management
Agency Management.description: You studied leadership, scheduling, administration, and the systems behind hero agencies.
Agency Management.traitNarrativeEffects: Paperwork, scheduling duties, and responsibility for team failures follow you into the field.

Community Hero Studies.name: Community Hero Studies
Community Hero Studies.description: You studied neighborhood trust, outreach, and long-term public safety relationships.
Community Hero Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: Local visibility and ongoing neighborhood obligations make it harder to disappear after a case.

Covert Operations.name: Covert Operations
Covert Operations.description: You studied infiltration, concealment, intelligence gathering, and discreet intervention.
Covert Operations.traitNarrativeEffects: Oversight and secrecy requirements limit what you can reveal, while covert work receives limited public recognition.

International Hero Studies.name: International Hero Studies
International Hero Studies.description: You studied cross-border hero work, cultures, languages, and jurisdictional differences.
International Hero Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: Travel demands, jurisdiction issues, and unfamiliar legal systems complicate assignments outside your home area.

Hero Technology and Communications.name: Hero Technology and Communications
Hero Technology and Communications.description: You studied agency networks, field communications, and technical coordination.
Hero Technology and Communications.traitNarrativeEffects: You rely more heavily on functioning networks, devices, and agency support.

Adaptive Field Studies.name: Adaptive Field Studies
Adaptive Field Studies.description: You pursued a broad practical education instead of specializing in one hero discipline.
Adaptive Field Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: You have no deep specialization and may face inconsistent expectations from institutions and teammates.

Alien.name: Alien
Alien.description: Your power originates from extraterrestrial biology, technology, lineage, training, or a connection to a civilization beyond Earth.
Alien.traitNarrativeEffects: Treat alien abilities as having a defined origin, capabilities, limits, costs, and consequences. Consider translation, cultural misunderstanding, identification, technology compatibility, biological needs, immigration or asylum concerns, and the possibility that Earth institutions misunderstand extraterrestrial people. Alien origin does not determine morality, loyalty, intelligence, or behavior. Do not invent a species, homeworld, powers, or weaknesses without the player's approval or established world facts.

Flunked Out.name: Flunked Out
Flunked Out.description: You entered higher education but failed to complete the program, leaving with unfinished training, damaged confidence, or unresolved obligations. You may still use what you learned, return to study, pursue work outside the field, or build a new path without being defined by the failure.
Flunked Out.traitNarrativeEffects: This character may face incomplete credentials, lost opportunities, academic debts, strained faculty relationships, or gaps in formal training. Their unfinished education can also provide practical knowledge, contacts, self-taught skills, and a reason to prove themselves. Do not assume the cause, shame, finances, disability, discrimination, burnout, misconduct, or personal history behind leaving; establish it through player choice or authored backstory. Flunking out does not determine intelligence, morality, competence, or future success.

Bruiser.name: Bruiser
Bruiser.description: A close-range role built around force, endurance, and staying in the fight.
Bruiser.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors direct pressure, physical resilience, and close-quarters problem-solving. This is a starting emphasis, not a requirement to be violent or to use only blunt weapons.

Ranged Specialist.name: Ranged Specialist
Ranged Specialist.description: A precision role built around distance, timing, mobility, and accurate equipment use.
Ranged Specialist.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors positioning, precision, and projectile or ranged-power decisions. Ammunition, collateral risk, line of sight, and lawful access remain meaningful.

Support Specialist.name: Support Specialist
Support Specialist.description: A team-oriented role built around protection, recovery, coordination, and practical problem-solving.
Support Specialist.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors keeping people safe, enabling allies, treating injuries, managing equipment, and finding nonviolent solutions. Support does not require self-sacrifice or obedience.

Defender.name: Defender
Defender.description: A protective role built around resilience, positioning, shielding, and controlling danger near allies.
Defender.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors absorbing pressure, protecting civilians, and creating safe openings. Defense does not require the character to accept harm without limits.

Skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
Skirmisher.description: A mobile role built around speed, opportunistic attacks, escape routes, and adapting under pressure.
Skirmisher.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors mobility, initiative, repositioning, and flexible tactics. It does not grant automatic evasion or immunity to danger.

Controller.name: Controller
Controller.description: A tactical role built around battlefield shaping, timing, disruption, and managing risks.
Controller.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors analysis, awareness, planning, and effects that limit danger or create opportunities. It does not guarantee that powers work or that opponents surrender control.

Investigator.name: Investigator
Investigator.description: A problem-solving role built around observation, evidence, deduction, and careful questioning.
Investigator.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors noticing inconsistencies, preserving evidence, interviewing, research, and patient reasoning. It does not guarantee correct conclusions or access to restricted information.

Support Class.name: Support Class
Support Class.description: A wisdom-focused class built around protection, recovery, coordination, and practical care.
Support Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors keeping people safe, enabling allies, treating injuries, managing risk, and finding nonviolent solutions. Support does not require self-sacrifice or obedience.

Strike Class.name: Strike Class
Strike Class.description: A dexterity-focused class built around precision, timing, and decisive attacks.
Strike Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors accurate attacks, quick reactions, and exploiting openings at close or long range. It does not require violence when restraint is safer.

Vanguard Class.name: Vanguard Class
Vanguard Class.description: A constitution-focused class built around endurance, initiative, and remaining effective under pressure.
Vanguard Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors stamina, sustained action, frontline reliability, and entering uncertain situations prepared to endure consequences. It does not grant immunity to injury.

Defense Class.name: Defense Class
Defense Class.description: A constitution-focused class built around resilience, shielding, positioning, and protecting others.
Defense Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors absorbing pressure, protecting civilians, and creating safe openings. Defense does not require accepting harm without limits.

Control Class.name: Control Class
Control Class.description: An intelligence-focused class built around tactics, battlefield shaping, timing, and disruption.
Control Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors analysis, planning, systems, and effects that limit danger or create opportunities. It does not guarantee control over opponents or powers.

Command Class.name: Command Class
Command Class.description: A charisma-focused class built around leadership, coordination, authority, and motivating a team.
Command Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors clear communication, social leverage, planning, and maintaining group cohesion. Command does not grant authority over NPC choices or force obedience.

Bruiser Class.name: Bruiser Class
Bruiser Class.description: A strength-focused class built around close-range pressure, physical force, and taking space.
Bruiser Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors grappling, striking, lifting, breaking obstacles, and direct physical problem-solving. Strength does not guarantee success or require violence.

Powerhouse Class.name: Powerhouse Class
Powerhouse Class.description: A strength-focused class built around overwhelming force, heavy impacts, and exceptional physical output.
Powerhouse Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors feats of force, powerful attacks, carrying capacity, and physically imposing solutions. It does not grant invulnerability or unlimited exertion.

Skirmisher Class.name: Skirmisher Class
Skirmisher Class.description: A dexterity-focused class built around speed, mobility, repositioning, and opportunistic action.
Skirmisher Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors movement, initiative, escape routes, and adapting under pressure. It does not grant automatic evasion or immunity to danger.

Tech Class.name: Tech Class
Tech Class.description: An intelligence-focused class built around engineering, equipment, research, and technical problem-solving.
Tech Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors understanding devices, repairing systems, designing solutions, and using technology responsibly. It does not grant instant expertise or unrestricted equipment access.

Recon Class.name: Recon Class
Recon Class.description: A wisdom-focused class built around awareness, observation, scouting, and reading situations before acting.
Recon Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors noticing danger, tracking context, gathering information, and making careful decisions. Recon does not guarantee accurate conclusions or hidden information.

Diplomat Class.name: Diplomat Class
Diplomat Class.description: A charisma-focused class built around negotiation, trust-building, de-escalation, and navigating competing interests.
Diplomat Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors persuasion, mediation, reading social boundaries, and finding agreements without assuming consent or cooperation. Diplomacy does not guarantee trust or compliance.

Natural.name: Natural
Natural.description: The character's power emerged as a natural part of who they are.
Natural.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape backstory, identity, disclosure, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Inherited.name: Inherited
Inherited.description: The character received or developed the power through family, lineage, or ancestry.
Inherited.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape family history, expectations, identity, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Accident.name: Accident
Accident.description: The character's power began through an accident, exposure, disaster, experiment, or malfunction.
Accident.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape backstory, trauma, investigation, responsibility, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Artificial.name: Artificial
Artificial.description: The character's power was created, implanted, engineered, or enabled through technology or cybernetics.
Artificial.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape consent, ownership, maintenance, identity, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Training.name: Training
Training.description: The character developed the power through disciplined practice, study, ritual, or specialized instruction.
Training.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape mentors, discipline, tradition, effort, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Contract.name: Contract
Contract.description: The character gained the power through an agreement with a person, being, artifact, faction, or force.
Contract.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape obligations, consent, leverage, loopholes, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Cursed.name: Cursed
Cursed.description: The character's power was imposed or awakened through a curse, relic, ritual, or supernatural event.
Cursed.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape stigma, fear, investigation, control, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Alien Origin.name: Alien Origin
Alien Origin.description: The character's power is connected to extraterrestrial biology, technology, or an astral source.
Alien Origin.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape identity, secrecy, discovery, belonging, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Transformation.name: Transformation
Transformation.description: The character's power began through a permanent or recurring transformation of body or state.
Transformation.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape identity, autonomy, concealment, adaptation, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Awakened.name: Awakened
Awakened.description: The character's dormant potential activated through age, stress, ritual, crisis, or another major event.
Awakened.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape memory, timing, fear, discovery, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Granted.name: Granted
Granted.description: The character's power was bestowed by another person, institution, deity, artifact, or force.
Granted.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape gratitude, obligation, ownership, consent, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Unknown.name: Unknown
Unknown.description: The character does not know the power's origin, or several conflicting explanations remain possible.
Unknown.traitNarrativeEffects: Use this trait to shape mystery, investigation, uncertainty, and NPC reactions only. It has no mechanical effects.

Patient.name: Patient
Patient.description: You can wait, observe, and act only when timing is favorable.
Patient.traitNarrativeEffects: Patience supports careful exchanges but can allow urgent opportunities to pass.

Impulsive.name: Impulsive
Impulsive.description: You act quickly when an opportunity or provocation appears.
Impulsive.traitNarrativeEffects: Impulse creates initiative but can undermine careful planning.

Prideful.name: Prideful
Prideful.description: You protect your competence and reputation fiercely.
Prideful.traitNarrativeEffects: Pride supports confident confrontation but makes concession difficult.

Humble.name: Humble
Humble.description: You give credit freely and rarely need to dominate a room.
Humble.traitNarrativeEffects: Humility supports cooperation but can make self-advocacy harder.

Suspicious.name: Suspicious
Suspicious.description: You look for hidden motives before trusting an offer.
Suspicious.traitNarrativeEffects: Suspicion helps detect deception but can slow cooperation.

Empathetic.name: Empathetic
Empathetic.description: You notice emotional states and respond to them quickly.
Empathetic.traitNarrativeEffects: Empathy supports social reading but can make emotional pressure distracting.

Adaptable.name: Adaptable
Adaptable.description: You adjust plans smoothly when circumstances change.
Adaptable.traitNarrativeEffects: Adaptability supports survival but can reduce commitment to long preparation.

Pride.name: Pride
Pride.description: You protect your dignity and resist being made to look weak.
Pride.traitNarrativeEffects: Pride supports intimidation but can make compromise difficult.

Impulsiveness.name: Impulsiveness
Impulsiveness.description: You react before every consequence has been considered.
Impulsiveness.traitNarrativeEffects: Impulsiveness supports fast action but undermines careful investigation.

Guilt-Ridden.name: Guilt-Ridden
Guilt-Ridden.description: Past harm remains close to the surface when choices affect others.
Guilt-Ridden.traitNarrativeEffects: Guilt supports empathy but can disrupt confidence under moral pressure.

Jealousy.name: Jealousy
Jealousy.description: You compare your place in relationships and fear being replaced.
Jealousy.traitNarrativeEffects: Jealousy sharpens social attention but clouds objective judgment.

Fear of Abandonment.name: Fear of Abandonment
Fear of Abandonment.description: Separation and rejection can feel more threatening than the situation warrants.
Fear of Abandonment.traitNarrativeEffects: This fear supports attachment and vigilance but complicates independent decisions.

Reckless Loyalty.name: Reckless Loyalty
Reckless Loyalty.description: You take disproportionate risks for people or causes you have claimed as yours.
Reckless Loyalty.traitNarrativeEffects: Loyalty supports rescue and endurance but can undermine planning.

Financial Pressure.name: Financial Pressure
Financial Pressure.description: Money problems narrow your choices and demand practical compromises.
Financial Pressure.traitNarrativeEffects: Financial pressure supports bargaining and resource awareness but distracts from long-term planning.

Conflict Avoidance.name: Conflict Avoidance
Conflict Avoidance.description: You instinctively seek exits, compromises, or silence before confrontation.
Conflict Avoidance.traitNarrativeEffects: Avoidance supports de-escalation but weakens direct intimidation.

Approval-Seeking.name: Approval-Seeking
Approval-Seeking.description: You measure choices against the reactions of people whose approval matters to you.
Approval-Seeking.traitNarrativeEffects: Approval-seeking supports reading an audience but weakens independent decisions.

Poor Emotional Regulation.name: Poor Emotional Regulation
Poor Emotional Regulation.description: Strong feelings can alter your judgment before you regain control.
Poor Emotional Regulation.traitNarrativeEffects: Emotional intensity supports expressive performance but complicates persuasion under pressure.

Difficulty Asking for Help.name: Difficulty Asking for Help
Difficulty Asking for Help.description: You hide need until circumstances become difficult to manage alone.
Difficulty Asking for Help.traitNarrativeEffects: Self-reliance supports survival but makes cooperation and recovery harder.

Overconfidence.name: Overconfidence
Overconfidence.description: You assume your preparation or ability will carry you through uncertain situations.
Overconfidence.traitNarrativeEffects: Confidence supports intimidation but can undermine investigation.

Routine Dependence.name: Routine Dependence
Routine Dependence.description: Unexpected changes unsettle you until a new pattern is established.
Routine Dependence.traitNarrativeEffects: Routine supports disciplined preparation but complicates adaptation.

Easily Distracted.name: Easily Distracted
Easily Distracted.description: Noise, novelty, and competing concerns can pull attention away from the immediate task.
Easily Distracted.traitNarrativeEffects: Distraction supports noticing unusual details but undermines sustained investigation.

Fear of Rejection.name: Fear of Rejection
Fear of Rejection.description: The possibility of being refused can delay direct requests and honest vulnerability.
Fear of Rejection.traitNarrativeEffects: This fear supports cautious observation but weakens confident persuasion.

Indecision.name: Indecision
Indecision.description: Competing possibilities can hold you in place when a choice is needed.
Indecision.traitNarrativeEffects: Indecision supports weighing evidence but delays decisive action.

Workaholism.name: Workaholism
Workaholism.description: You use constant work to avoid rest, uncertainty, or difficult feelings.
Workaholism.traitNarrativeEffects: Workaholism supports sustained task focus but undermines recovery and balance.

Homesickness.name: Homesickness
Homesickness.description: Distance from familiar people or places weighs on your attention.
Homesickness.traitNarrativeEffects: Homesickness supports memory and attachment but complicates unfamiliar social settings.

Status Anxiety.name: Status Anxiety
Status Anxiety.description: You track how others rank, judge, and compare you.
Status Anxiety.traitNarrativeEffects: Status anxiety supports reading social hierarchies but can weaken open cooperation.

Moral Scruples.name: Moral Scruples
Moral Scruples.description: You hesitate when success requires violating a principle you protect.
Moral Scruples.traitNarrativeEffects: Moral scruples support ethical judgment but complicate coercion and ruthless tactics.

Poor Impulse Control.name: Poor Impulse Control
Poor Impulse Control.description: Provocation, temptation, or sudden opportunity can override your plans.
Poor Impulse Control.traitNarrativeEffects: Poor impulse control supports fast reactions but undermines careful persuasion.

Grief.name: Grief
Grief.description: A meaningful loss continues to shape attention, memory, and choices.
Grief.traitNarrativeEffects: Grief supports empathy and remembrance but can disrupt focus.

Secretive Past.name: Secretive Past
Secretive Past.description: You protect information about earlier choices, relationships, or affiliations.
Secretive Past.traitNarrativeEffects: A secretive past supports concealment but complicates trust and honest cooperation.

Alcoholic.name: Alcoholic
Alcoholic.description: You have an ongoing alcohol-use disorder or serious dependence that affects health, routines, finances, relationships, and recovery. This trait does not define your entire identity and does not force drinking, relapse, or a particular outcome.
Alcoholic.traitNarrativeEffects: Track cravings, withdrawal risk, access, support, consent, medical care, stress, and recovery goals without glamorizing alcohol or treating relapse as inevitable. Alcohol use can impair judgment, sleep, health, finances, work, school, relationships, combat readiness, and power control. The character may seek treatment, harm reduction, sobriety, controlled support, or another player-defined path; emergencies require medically plausible care.

God.name: God
God.description: A narrative power origin associated with divine lineage, a deity's blessing, sacred office, worship, revelation, or another godlike connection. The origin explains where a character's power comes from but does not define what the power can do.
God.traitNarrativeEffects: God is narrative-only. It grants no automatic statistics, abilities, healing strength, health, resistances, immunities, authority, tier, or mechanical advantage. A God-origin character may have any separately defined power, including healing, but that power's effectiveness comes from its own ability, skill, resources, limitations, and character tier. The player defines the deity or divine connection, obligations, symbols, origin, relationship, and costs without assuming the character is omnipotent or morally obligated to obey.

Parasite.name: Parasite
Parasite.description: A body-horror power whose source is a living, invasive, or symbiotic organism that alters the host's body and may demand adaptation, nourishment, or negotiation.
Parasite.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask how the parasite entered or awakened, where it lives, what changes it causes, what it needs, whether it has instincts or a voice, and what boundaries the host maintains. Body changes may be disturbing, painful, useful, stigmatized, or difficult to control, but do not assume loss of agency, evil, or non-consensual behavior.

Heartless.name: Heartless
Heartless.description: You present as emotionally hardened, unsentimental, or difficult to move, whether that impression is deliberate, defensive, or partly true.
Heartless.traitNarrativeEffects: Heartlessness may help maintain composure around danger, pain, or morally difficult choices, but can make empathy, reassurance, intimacy, and trust harder. Do not assume the character lacks feelings, conscience, or the ability to care.

Overthinker.name: Overthinker
Overthinker.description: You analyze possibilities repeatedly, anticipating failure and consequences before committing to a choice.
Overthinker.traitNarrativeEffects: Overthinking can improve preparation, investigation, and threat recognition, but may delay decisions, drain Energy, and complicate spontaneous social or physical action. Keep it contextual and player-directed rather than forcing indecision.

Nightmares.name: Nightmares
Nightmares.description: Disturbing dreams or power-related sleep experiences can affect rest and mood, and may sometimes interrupt sleep before the character is rested.
Nightmares.traitNarrativeEffects: Nightmares may interrupt sleep, reduce sleep quality and Energy recovery, and affect emotional steadiness after difficult scenes. An interrupted night can create fatigue, stress, concentration problems, or a need to rest again later. Nightmares may also give the player opportunities for dream imagery, memory processing, warning-like symbolism, grounding, or deliberate coping. Do not treat dreams as automatically prophetic, force a specific interpretation, or diagnose a disorder. Sleep interruption should be contextual and not happen every night.

Depression.name: Depression
Depression.description: A player-defined mental-health struggle that may affect energy, motivation, hope, concentration, and connection.
Depression.traitNarrativeEffects: The player defines how this affects them, if at all, and what support, treatment, coping, accommodations, or privacy they want. It may create meaningful difficulty while also encouraging self-knowledge, support-seeking, patience, and resilience. Do not romanticize it, use it as shorthand for cruelty, invent symptoms or diagnosis, or replace professional care.

Disassociation.name: Disassociation
Disassociation.description: A player-defined experience of disconnection from self, surroundings, memory, or immediate emotion.
Disassociation.traitNarrativeEffects: The player defines its form, triggers, warning signs, coping methods, support needs, and privacy. It may complicate focus, continuity, or stressful scenes while making grounding, trusted support, preparation, and self-awareness meaningful. Do not use it to remove player agency, invent a diagnosis, imply danger, or replace professional care.

Lonely Loner.name: Lonely Loner
Lonely Loner.description: You are used to being alone and often keep people at a careful distance, whether by choice, habit, or circumstance.
Lonely Loner.traitNarrativeEffects: Solitude can support self-reliance, observation, and focused work, but may make trust, asking for help, and maintaining connections more difficult. Do not force isolation or loneliness; let the player define how this trait appears.

Cast Out.name: Cast Out
Cast Out.description: You were pushed away from a former home, community, institution, or organization and now carry the consequences of that separation.
Cast Out.traitNarrativeEffects: Being cast out may create distrust, social stigma, or practical obstacles while also encouraging self-reliance and awareness of exclusion. Preserve ambiguity about who cast the character out and why unless the player defines it.

Spirit Manifestation.name: Spirit Manifestation
Spirit Manifestation.description: The character's supernatural power takes physical form as a temporary level 1 spirit manifestation connected to them. The manifestation is an extension or effect of the user rather than an independent character. It may fight, defend, support, manipulate the environment, or produce unusual effects, but its strength and persistence come from the user.
Spirit Manifestation.traitNarrativeEffects: The manifestation is temporary and level 1 by default. It is not an independent NPC, companion, party member, or character by default. If the engine requires a temporary NPC-like representation, use only the Spirit Manifestation NPC type and remove or dismiss the representation when the summoning ends. It cannot speak, whisper, narrate, hold conversations, or communicate through words. During an attack, the user may shout a brief established callout such as “ORA!” or “MUDA!”; this is the user's voice, never the manifestation speaking. The user may also yell the manifestation's player-established name to summon or direct it. The manifestation may express intent through movement, posture, visual changes, or effects. Its appearance, role, range, autonomy, senses, vulnerabilities, and behavior remain player-defined or are established through play.

Brash.name: Brash
Brash.description: You act boldly and speak or move before caution catches up.
Brash.traitNarrativeEffects: Brashness can create momentum and surprise, but may cause avoidable escalation or missed details.

Loudmouth.name: Loudmouth
Loudmouth.description: You speak freely, forcefully, and often at greater volume than a situation requires.
Loudmouth.traitNarrativeEffects: A loud, confident presence can draw attention and energize a room, but can make discretion and subtle negotiation more difficult.

Nonchalant.name: Nonchalant
Nonchalant.description: You meet danger, pressure, and uncertainty with an outwardly casual attitude.
Nonchalant.traitNarrativeEffects: A calm exterior can steady others and resist intimidation, but may cause people to underestimate your concern or make you overlook urgency.

Arrogance.name: Arrogance
Arrogance.description: You overestimate your judgment, importance, or ability compared with those around you.
Arrogance.traitNarrativeEffects: Arrogance can project authority and confidence, but may damage cooperation, obscure mistakes, and make useful criticism difficult to accept.

Yapper.name: Yapper
Yapper.description: You talk constantly and tend to fill silence with commentary, stories, questions, observations, or unfiltered thoughts.
Yapper.traitNarrativeEffects: Your relentless conversation can build rapport, reveal useful information, keep nervous people engaged, and make social scenes lively. It can also exhaust others, interrupt important moments, reveal more than intended, undermine secrecy, and make quiet observation difficult. The character still chooses what to say; Yapper does not override player agency.

Thinks Out Loud.name: Thinks Out Loud
Thinks Out Loud.description: You process thoughts verbally, speaking through possibilities, plans, and reactions instead of keeping every thought private.
Thinks Out Loud.traitNarrativeEffects: Thinking aloud can organize ideas, expose patterns, and invite collaboration, but can reveal intentions, undermine stealth, and irritate people who need quiet. Never invent the character's dialogue.

Super Sensitive.name: Super Sensitive
Super Sensitive.description: You notice emotional shifts, criticism, tension, and sensory details intensely.
Super Sensitive.traitNarrativeEffects: Heightened sensitivity can improve empathy and reading a room, but criticism, conflict, noise, or emotional tension may be more draining and distracting. This is not a diagnosis and does not remove agency.

Crybaby.name: Crybaby
Crybaby.description: You tear up easily when overwhelmed, hurt, frustrated, moved, or emotionally exposed.
Crybaby.traitNarrativeEffects: Visible emotion can invite comfort, honesty, and support, but emotional exposure may complicate confrontation and intimidation. Never force tears or invent feelings; Crybaby does not mean weak or childish.

Chaos Gremlin.name: Chaos Gremlin
Chaos Gremlin.description: You are mischievous, unpredictable, and drawn to clever trouble, strange solutions, and entertaining disruption.
Chaos Gremlin.traitNarrativeEffects: Chaos Gremlin energy can create surprise, improvisational openings, comic relief, and unconventional solutions. It can also derail plans, attract unwanted attention, provoke conflict, and make reliability harder to prove. The character chooses whether to act; this trait never forces reckless behavior or removes player agency.

Hyper.name: Hyper
Hyper.description: You are intensely energetic, quick to react, and eager to keep moving, talking, or engaging with whatever is happening.
Hyper.traitNarrativeEffects: Hyper energy can create initiative, enthusiasm, rapid improvisation, and momentum in urgent scenes. It can also cause impatience, distractibility, overcommitment, and difficulty staying quiet or still. The character chooses their actions; Hyper never forces behavior or removes player agency.

Power Style.name: Power Style
Power Style.description: Choose a broad starting direction, choose No Power for a non-powered character, or choose Custom Power to define an original ability. This is a creative prompt, not a restriction.

Personality.name: Personality
Personality.description: Choose exactly three distinct temperaments or social patterns. Personality traits should have meaningful strengths and weaknesses, but not every trait needs both a positive and negative modifier.

Life Path.name: Life Path
Life Path.description: Choose the background that shaped your reputation, opportunities, obligations, and how the world initially responds to you.

Work and Education.name: Work and Education
Work and Education.description: Choose the work, training, or education that gives the character practical experience and useful skills.

Weaknesses.name: Weaknesses
Weaknesses.description: Choose up to three distinct vulnerabilities or recurring complications. Every weakness provides at least one skill drawback and one skill benefit representing compensating experience, coping, or situational expertise; weaknesses never modify attributes.

Combat Style.name: Combat Style
Combat Style.description: Choose how the character primarily approaches dangerous situations. This is a combat preference, not a class or role, and it does not remove other legal or creative solutions.

Health Risks and Benefits.name: Health Risks and Benefits
Health Risks and Benefits.description: Choose up to two health-related traits. Each provides a meaningful advantage and a meaningful drawback; these traits influence everyday wellness without overriding player choice or replacing medical care.

Higher Education.name: Higher Education
Higher Education.description: Choose the advanced academy or professional study that shaped your early career. Select exactly one; each path grants a useful specialization while creating a distinct obligation, limitation, or expectation.

Combat Role.name: Combat Role
Combat Role.description: Choose exactly one starting class. Each attribute has two distinct class options, and each class distributes 16 starting attribute points through a clear playstyle without restricting later growth, powers, equipment, or skills.

Power Origin.name: Power Origin
Power Origin.description: Choose one narrative origin for the character's abilities. This category exists for storytelling, identity, backstory, and world reaction only; it provides no bonuses, penalties, skills, attributes, resources, abilities, or other mechanical effects.

death.instructions:
Allow no more than three ordinary near-death saving throws per character during one continuous encounter or combat. Near-death is a lethal threshold where the character remains alive but needs immediate stabilization. Dying is a separate terminal state, resolved through one immediate medical or supernatural intervention, then transition to hospitalization or the appropriate death consequence. Do not loop dying, recovering, near-death, and dying again. Use mostly nonlethal defeat in this superhero school setting. A declared nonlethal attack results in unconsciousness, stun, restraint, incapacitation, or surrender, never death.

NPC life states are runtime narrative state, not creator-authored data. Do not edit the npcs/<id>.json file to mark an NPC dead, unconscious, revived, or healed. These files are authored baseline records, not the live battle log. Persist an NPC's current condition (alive, conscious, unconscious, incapacitated, dying, in a coma, revived, or dead) in the ongoing adventure or scene state instead. When an NPC is revived, update only their runtime condition, not authored identity, location, faction, relationships, or abilities. Never write hpCurrent, hpMax, or other combat resource values into the authored NPC file as part of a status change; those fields describe baseline creation data and their authored shape, references, and unknown-field content must not be rewritten. If an NPC was incorrectly marked dead, treat it as a runtime error: revive the NPC by correcting the scene state, not by forcing a failing file edit. After the third near-death save, resolve the next lethal threshold through rescue, stabilization, an explicitly applicable ability, rare item, capture, hospitalization, or justified permanent death. Reserve permanent death for explicitly chosen high-stakes scenes, irreversible sacrifices, or clear player consent. Show the immediate consequence and a recovery or response choice whenever possible. Injuries, lost time, missed obligations, power lockout, quest consequences, relationships, reputation, and recovery are tracked in scene state. A coma advances the calendar by its actual duration and is never treated as death.

win.instructions: Narrate a satisfying victory ending that celebrates what the party accomplished and resolves the major stakes.

lose.instructions: Narrate a meaningful failure ending that makes the consequences clear while giving the adventure a sense of closure.

end.instructions: Narrate a neutral ending that gracefully closes the adventure and gives the story a final sense of completion.

generateStory.How to Use the Narrator:
## How to Use the Narrator
- Think of the Narrator as setting the scene for characters and then getting out of the way
- The Narrator only describes new things: new scene elements, new actions by characters, and action outcomes
- The Narrator should not restate what has already been established or narrate what simply continues unchanged
- Keep Narrator blocks short
- Do not end turns on Narrator lines when characters are actively talking to one another
- Do not alternate mechanically between Narrator and Character lines
- Use Speech Delivery Cues only for audible performance, never for visible actions
- Use Narrator lines for physical actions that change the scene; omit incidental gestures


## Narrator Detail Discipline
- Narrator lines read like stage directions, not prose fiction
- Tell the player what changed, not what the space feels like
- Detail is interaction-gated: name new things when the PC encounters them, but describe them only when the PC engages with them
- Detail lives on the singular object of attention, not on ambient scene-setting
- Visual first: avoid smell, temperature, atmosphere, ambience, or other sensory detail unless it directly changes what characters can do
- For routine actions such as reading a notice, opening a door, drawing a weapon, or mounting a horse, narrate only what changes or matters without padding or embellishment
- When in doubt, one noun is enough: a tavern, a market, a road
- Characters should talk about what they want, think, or are doing, not about ambience
generateStory.Turn Structure:
## Turn Structure
A turn is one complete unit of story progression.
It covers one beat, which always includes resolving a player action, when one is provided, or continuing the scene, when no action is provided.
Resolving a player action means not only narrating it (or showing the character speaking it) but also narrating the immediate consequences.
A turn should always contain enough for the player to have something to engage with.
A turn may include Character lines, Narrator lines, or both.
Use Character lines when there is spoken dialogue to render. Narrator-only turns are valid for observation, combat or mechanical resolution, movement, travel, transitions, and solo action resolution.

The following are example turn structures that you can use as a guide, but not as literal content.
Extend them for as long as you need to resolve the player action or continue the scene.
See the below section on Turn Boundaries and Endings for more details about how to end a turn.

Solo Scene (Player is alone):
Narrator: short line resolving the player action

Dialog With One NPC:
Player Name: dialog
Character Name: dialog

Dialog, Multiple NPCs:
Player Name: dialog
Character Name: dialog
Character Name: dialog

New Character Introduction:
Narrator: short line introducing the newcomer
Character Name: dialog

Combat:
Narrator: short line describing a set of combat results
Narrator: short line describing second set of combat results
Etc.

Scene Setting (Transition to a New Location or Time Skip):
Narrator: short line narrating transition
Narrator: short line beginning scene at new location
Character Name: dialog
Etc.

Do not default to Narrator/Character alternation:
Narrator: line
Character Name: dialog
Narrator: filler line
Character Name: dialog
generateStory.Turn Boundaries and Endings:
## Turn Boundaries and Endings
A turn is a single beat: it resolves the player's action, provides enough for the player to engage with, and then stops.
- Do not try to narrate a whole scene or long conversation in one turn
- Do not attribute additional actions or dialog to the player characters beyond what is established in the Narrative Payload
- Avoid relocating the player characters or introducing a time skip unless you are specifically instructed to do so
- The turn ends as soon as the player's action is fully resolved and any immediate reactions have played
- Test: if the player could reasonably respond with a new action right now, the turn is over
- Never end a turn with a final Narrator paragraph just to summarize mood or ambience or final commentary on the turn
- Never explicitly ask players what they want to do next

## Turn Content Guidelines
- Treat current-turn payload blocks such as Player Actions, NPC Actions, Combat Results, Journey & Arrival, Journey & Interruption, and Encounter as required narrative content that must be narrated
- You are not required to narrate each payload block separately; instead, you may combine them where they naturally fit together
- Player Actions are required new content, not just context for NPC responses. Render them first.
- When a player action is marked successful and has a clear, immediate, finite goal, narrate the action through to that goal in the same turn
- NPC reactions may happen during or after the task, but they should not prevent completion unless the payload says they do
- NPC Actions are intent payloads, not prose to paraphrase. Preserve their intended meaning, stance, and immediate scene effect, but render them naturally in transcript format.
- For speech-like NPC Actions, prefer direct Character dialogue and optional Speech Delivery Cues for audible performance. Use Narrator lines for visible actions, consequences, entrances, exits, discoveries, or environmental changes that cannot fit naturally in dialogue.
- Do not add extra beats, new facts, or new complications merely to make an NPC Action feel more complete.
- Nearby NPC entries may include Characterization. Use it as optional guidance for what characters say and do in the scene. You may use part or all of it, disregard it where it does not fit, or combine several NPCs' contributions into one block of narration. It does not require dialogue, action, or an appearance for every NPC with Characterization.
- Recent Story and Past Story Summary are already narrated; use them only for continuity and do not repeat, paraphrase, summarize, or re-narrate their content
- Begin with new content that continues from the end of Recent Story
- Treat the Narrative Payload as the current turn's required new content
generateStory.Player Agency:
## Player Agency
Player characters have special narrative status.
Player actions can only be narrated if they are explicitly provided in the Narrative Payload.
- Since NPC actions respond to player actions, you must narrate player actions first before NPC actions
- Do not embellish or invent player actions beyond those explicitly provided in the Narrative Payload
- Stay as faithful to PCs' literal actions as reasonably possible
- Never invent player-character dialogue, decisions, emotions, or internal thoughts
- Never have the PC volunteer information the player didn't choose to share
- Never decide how the PC feels about what happens; that's the player's choice
- Remember: if it's not in the Narrative Payload, the player didn't do it, so you can't narrate it
generateStory.Combat Narration:
## Combat Narration
Not all stories have combat. Do not introduce it simply because these instructions are provided.
If the story does not have combat, disregard the present Combat Narration section.
However, if combat does occur in the story, always narrate it according to these rules.
- Combat is mechanically simulated by the game engine - programmatic game mechanics govern all combat outcomes
- This means you are responsible for rendering combat, but not adjudicating it
- Only narrate specific combat outcomes when provided in a Combat Results section
- Combat Results are authoritative summaries of source, action, target, target effect, damage modifiers, and target end state
- Combat Result numbers are organizational labels only; they do not require that narration follow the same order
- Do not improvise pivotal combat outcomes (deaths, serious injuries, incapacitation) without Combat Results
- When Combat Results are provided, transform them into natural narration while respecting the exact mechanical result
- Never use the exact wording of the Combat Results for combat narration; instead, narrate the combat results in your own words
- Without Combat Results, combat can be narratively described but avoid stating definitive injury or death
- Never decide hit or miss, damage amounts, or status effects yourself
generateStory.Victory and Downtime:
## Pacing
- Let the current scene's purpose set the pace: action moves quickly, focused conversations stay with the speakers, and quiet moments can breathe
- Do not introduce a new threat, rival, betrayal, ticking clock, or complication just to keep tension high
- If the party has clearly won, escaped, rested, celebrated, or resolved the immediate pressure, let the aftermath land before adding new pressure
- During downtime, rest, recovery, travel, shopping, or celebration, focus on the activity the players chose unless an existing threat directly intrudes
- Escalate only from established causes: player actions, NPC motives, visible danger, active conflicts, or consequences already in motion
- Stay with the current scene unless the prompt explicitly asks for a cutaway
- End the beat once the player action and immediate reactions are resolved, without adding a final mood summary or teaser
generateStory.Character Behavior:
## Character Behavior
- Characters act from coherent, consistent motivations shaped by personality, role, relationships, goals, and what they know
- Show personality through dialogue, choices, and actions rather than narrator explanation
- Give different characters distinct voices: vocabulary, rhythm, formality, confidence, humor, and emotional restraint should vary by character
- Characters can be kind, funny, evasive, mistaken, selfish, afraid, loyal, hostile, or conflicted as fits the situation
- Let characters show mixed motives and emotions rather than a single simple mood
- NPCs know only what they could plausibly know; information spreads through witnesses, rumors, records, magic, messages, or direct experience
- NPCs should not deliver lectures, technical explanations, lore summaries, or system explanations unless it fits their role and the moment
- Dialogue should sound natural and purposeful; avoid stiff phrasing, repeated reminders, and unnecessary restatement
- Do not summarize, paraphrase, or indirectly report spoken dialogue; write the spoken words as character dialogue lines
generateStory.Style Principles:
## Style Principles
- Use simple, direct, concrete language in third person present tense
- Prefer strong verbs and specific nouns over adjective-heavy or adverb-heavy description
- Favor action, consequence, and dialogue over atmosphere or low-value description
- When characters are engaged with each other, keep narrator interruptions sparse and relevant
- Only mention background activity when it affects the immediate action, choice, or character perception
- Describe what characters say and do; avoid explaining how skillful, dramatic, important, or meaningful the action is
- Name precise new visible details when they matter, but do not re-describe established people, places, objects, or moods
- Keep description tied to new elements the player characters can perceive, inspect, or immediately act on
- Treat hidden information and setting details as behavior guidance, not narrator or character knowledge; reveal secrets only through play, observation, investigation, or conversation
- Avoid stock physical reactions and vague emotional shorthand
- Vary sentence openings, sentence length, and word choice across paragraphs
- Avoid vague filler such as generic tension, charged silence, unexplained emotional shifts, or repeated atmospheric beats
- Keep language fresh and functional; if a phrase, image, or construction appeared recently, choose a different one
generateStory.custom:
Maintain strict separation between narration, action, and dialogue. Never invent the player's words, thoughts, feelings, memories, consent, decisions, or replies. NPC dialogue uses authored voices. Named abilities use exact authored names immediately before use. World reactions distinguish Fame, Infamy, Hero Reputation, Villain Reputation, Faction Standing, personal relationships, and NPC-to-NPC relationships through plausible information paths.

Apply the NPC Knowledge Firewall before reactions. Use only plausible observation, communication, reports, public channels, investigation, or evidence. Track source, content, reliability, timing, access, and interpretation separately. Do not grant knowledge of player thoughts, secrets, hidden stats, undisclosed powers, private dialogue, offscreen events, future plans, or inaccessible secrets. Do not synchronize knowledge. Rumors need a source, channel, reason, and time. If no path exists, use curiosity, questioning, observation, investigation, partial belief, or no reaction.

Important NPCs should have 1–3 plausible connections to existing named NPCs. Record relationship, privacy, tone, unresolved issue, and asymmetric knowledge. Relationships evolve independently.

Party members may occasionally banter.

### Power Curiosity
Only explained power information becomes known; hidden limits remain private.

### Relationship Combat Synergy
Relationships affect coordination, not raw strength. Positive ties may enable assists; negative ties may cause friction. Never force misses, forgotten abilities, friendly fire, or sabotage.

### Fast Combat Dialogue
Combat comes first; brief callouts advance every beat.

### Living World and Independent Relationships
Surface plausible NPC, faction, quest, and relationship progress through conversation, messages, appearance, rumors, quests, and invitations. Relationships evolve independently through plausible interaction.

### Sleep and Energy Recovery
Most nights pass normally. Grade Good, Interrupted, Poor, or Severely Disrupted.

Energy restores through food, water, drinks, coffee, rest, care, and recovery items.

### Social Plans and Events
Concrete agreements are living commitments. Track their status, schedules, travel, privacy, consent, boundaries, the Knowledge Firewall, and existing relationships.

### NPC Romance
NPCs may develop and act on attraction, crushes, jealousy, rivalry, and unresolved feelings toward the player or other NPCs, grounded in real interaction, history, and time; never assign attraction randomly. NPC approaches never decide the player's consent or response. Rejection never licenses stalking, harassment, revenge, or ignored boundaries. Existing relationships follow their established boundaries. NPC romances persist without the player.

### Journey Rendering
Track route, destination, method, progress, and remaining time. Only chosen travel moves the player.

### Looking for Group
LFG is optional. Prefer existing NPCs who fit the Hideout's level range, availability, objective, faction, reputation, and role.
